items.title: Lightweight UAV-based object detection and tracking for intelligent oil and gas field safety monitoring
items.abstract: Continuous, reliable monitoring of geographically dispersed oil and gas production facilities is essential for accident prevention, asset integrity, and regulatory compliance, yet ground-based inspection is labour-intensive and temporally sparse. Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) offer on-demand aerial coverage, but automated interpretation of production-site imagery is hindered by extreme target-scale variation, irregular equipment geometries, and the limited compute available on airborne platforms. This paper presents an integrated lightweight detection-and-tracking framework tailored to oil and gas field surveillance. The detector augments YOLOv8s with deformable C2f (DCNv2) modules for geometry-adaptive feature extraction, a progressive feature pyramid (AFPN) that suppresses cross-scale semantic conflict, a parameter-shared detail-enhanced head (LSDECD-Head), a Focaler-GIoU regression loss, and LAMP structured pruning for embedded deployment. For dynamic situational awareness, an improved ByteTrack introduces a spatial-appearance similarity matrix encoding operational-state cues and an acceleration-aware Kalman correction. On VisDrone2019, UAVDT, and a self-constructed oil-and-gas dataset (OGF-UAV), the method attains 44.1%, 57.6%, and 56.3% mAP@0.5 with only 7.8 M parameters at 78 FPS, and reduces tracking identity switches by up to 43.2%. The pruned model runs at 18.3 FPS on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX 16 GB under TensorRT FP16, confirming practicality for real-time field deployment.

items.title: LLMs can assist with proposal selection at large user facilities
items.abstract: Abstract We explore how large language models (LLMs) can enhance the proposal selection process at large user facilities, offering a scalable, consistent, and cost-effective alternative to traditional human review. Proposal selection depends on assessing the relative strength among submitted proposals; however, traditional human scoring often suffers from weak inter-proposal correlations and is subject to reviewer bias and inconsistency. A pairwise preference-based approach is logically superior, providing a more rigorous and internally consistent basis for ranking, but its quadratic workload makes it impractical for human reviewers. We address this limitation using LLMs. Leveraging the uniquely well-curated proposals and publication records from three beamlines at the Spallation Neutron Source (SNS), Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL), we show that the LLM rankings correlate strongly with the human rankings (Spearman $$\rho \simeq 0.2-0.8$$ , improving to $$\ge 0.5$$ after 10% outlier removal). Moreover, LLM performance is no worse than that of human reviewers in identifying proposals with high publication potential, while costing over two orders of magnitude less. Beyond ranking, LLMs enable advanced analyses that are challenging for humans, such as quantitative assessment of proposal similarity via embedding models, which provides information crucial for review committees.

items.title: Longitudinal associations of occupational cumulative noise exposure duration and hearing loss with lipid profiles: a 9-year cohort study
items.abstract: Background Occupational noise exposure causes auditory damage and is also closely associated with systemic metabolic abnormalities. The impact of long-term noise exposure on longitudinal lipid changes remains unclear. Objective This longitudinal study examined the association of baseline cumulative noise exposure duration with serum triglycerides (TG) and total cholesterol (TC) in male workers, and further examined whether binaural high-frequency average hearing threshold (BHFTA), an objective marker of noise-induced cochlear damage, modified longitudinal lipid trends. Methods In this retrospective longitudinal cohort study, 431 male workers were followed for 9 years. Occupational noise exposure was defined according to the Chinese national standard GBZ/T 224-2010 as exposure to an 8-hour equivalent continuous A-weighted sound level of at least 80 dB(A) (Lex, 8h), and was operationalized as the cumulative duration of employment in noise-exposed positions ascertained from plant administrative records. Linear mixed-effects models were used to analyze the effects of follow-up time, baseline cumulative noise exposure duration (mean-centered, time-invariant), and their interaction on natural log-transformed TG and TC, adjusted for age, body mass index, lipid-lowering medication use, smoking, and alcohol consumption. Simple slopes were estimated at representative exposure durations (3, 10, and 20 years). Because individual biological noise dose could not be directly measured, BHFTA was used as an objective marker of accumulated biological dose and individual susceptibility in sensitivity analyses, with simple slopes estimated at BHFTA values of mean ± 1 standard deviation (SD). Results Baseline cumulative noise exposure duration was significantly and positively associated with serum TG levels, with each additional year of exposure corresponding to an approximately 2.0% higher TG level (β = 0.0203 per year on ln(TG), 95% CI: 0.0029–0.0377, P = 0.022), whereas its association with TC did not reach statistical significance ( P = 0.077). The follow-up time and baseline exposure duration interaction was negative in direction, that is, the annual rate of lipid increase tended to be smaller among workers with longer baseline exposure; this reached borderline significance for TG (β = −0.0013, 95% CI: −0.0027–0.0001, P = 0.066) and statistical non-significance for TC ( P = 0.479). The estimated annual TG increase displayed a monotonic descriptive gradient across baseline exposure duration of 3, 10, and 20 years (5.35%, 4.39%, and 3.03% per year, respectively). In sensitivity analyses, BHFTA interacted positively with follow-up time for both outcomes (TG: 0.0023, 95% CI: 0.0013–0.0034; TC: 0.0005, 95% CI: 0.0001–0.0009); the estimated annual increase rose from 2.07 to 4.61% for TG and from 0.73 to 1.28% for TC as BHFTA increased from mean – 1 SD to mean + 1 SD (14.3–24.9 dB). Conclusions Baseline cumulative noise exposure duration was associated with elevated TG levels, and the attenuated rate of lipid increase over time may partly reflect a healthy worker survivor effect. In contrast, BHFTA may be more sensitive than administrative exposure records in revealing the metabolic consequences of chronic noise exposure. Hearing conservation and metabolic monitoring should be integrated into occupational health surveillance.

items.title: Managers Who Build and Managers Who Break: Abusive Supervision, Psychological Safety, and Team Learning-A Critical Review of the Evidence and Its Limits
items.abstract: In normal language, it's just one word that makes the difference between a manager and a damager, but the difference in behaviour between the two can be measured in the learning of the team, the health of the staff and the cost to the organisation. This article examines peer-reviewed journal evidence pertaining to supervisory behavior, including studies on abusive supervision, psychological safety, just culture in safety critical industries, and occupational health research that relates supervisors' ratings to reported illness. These can be found in occupational medicine cohort studies, regulatory text on error reporting and the use of data in the workplace, and in organisational behaviour journals and international standards on psychosocial risk. Three findings recur. First, teams which have leaders who ask how when things go wrong report more problems and make earlier corrections than teams with leaders who ask who. Second, hostile supervision is positively related to turnover intentions, decreased task performance and poorer health, with most designs being based on employee perception and there is limited ability to determine cause and effect. Third, the published figures of cost of damaging supervision are less convincing than the fact that they are frequently cited is sometimes thought to indicate. This article outlines the current measurement options, the legal parameters for their use, and practical options for employers, regulators, and employees. The evidence of causation and cross-country data are still relatively scarce.

items.title: Marker-Less Augmented Reality as a Catalyst for Digital Transformation in Furniture SMEs Through an Extension of the Cognitive–Affective–Conative Theory
items.abstract: While large firms of furniture industry have integrated technologies such as Augmented Reality (AR) to allow consumers to visualize 3D furniture in their own spaces before purchase, small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) have not yet fully optimized this technology. This study examines consumer acceptance of AR in the SME furniture sector by developing a prototype product catalog website that integrates AR functionality. It also introduces a new theoretical model, the Cognitive, Affective, Evaluative, Conative (CAEC) model, which extends the traditional Cognitive, Affective, Conative (CAC) theory by adding an evaluative stage. A mixed-methods approach is employed, combining semi-structured interviews and surveys with the AR-enabled website prototype. The research contributes theoretically by introducing the CAEC model and provides a refined framework for understanding technology adoption. Practically, it guides SMEs in enhancing consumer engagement and purchase intentions through the use of AR.

items.title: Más Allá de la Salud: Modelo Integral de Felicidad, Bienestar y Florecimiento Humano
items.abstract: Objective: To substantiate a multidimensional model that expands health toward happiness, well-being, and flourishing by integrating personal, relational, material, and digital factors. Methodology: A theoretical-propositional study supported by an integrative review of the biopsychosocial model, subjective and eudaimonic well-being, self-determination, positive psychology, meaning, social determinants, capabilities, occupational health, and digital well-being. Results: The Integral Model of Human Well-Being with Soul (MIBHA) is formulated around eight dimensions—body, thought, emotions, transcendence, social life, professional life, finances, and technology—and five cross-cutting mechanisms: resources, agency, regulation, connection, and meaning. A theory of change, ten propositions, a preliminary 40-item scale, indicators, implementation phases, and ethical safeguards are developed. Conclusions: Well-being cannot be reduced to a score, an individual habit, or the absence of disease. It requires real capabilities, fair environments, and responsible governance. MIBHA offers a testable basis for research and intervention without replacing clinical diagnosis or treatment. Its original contribution lies in separating life domains from cross-cutting mechanisms, treating technology as a constitutive dimension, and introducing a non-compensation principle for severe deprivation.

items.title: Menopausal Symptom Burden and Self-Reported Poor Sleep Quality Among Japanese Working Women Aged 40 Years and Older: An Exploratory Cross-Sectional Study
items.abstract: Background and Objectives: Sleep-related complaints are common among women in midlife and may reflect not only insufficient sleep duration but also broader menopausal symptom burden. Although menopausal symptoms and sleep problems are known to be related, less is known about how menopausal symptom domains are associated with self-reported sleep quality among working women, particularly when objective sleep duration is considered. This exploratory cross-sectional study aimed to examine the association between menopausal symptom burden and self-reported poor sleep quality among Japanese working women aged 40 years and older, while accounting for objectively measured sleep duration. Materials and Methods: Participants completed questionnaires on sleep quality and menopausal symptoms and underwent objective sleep monitoring using a wearable electroencephalography device. Self-reported sleep quality was assessed using an item corresponding to the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index and dichotomized into poor and good sleep quality. Menopausal symptoms were evaluated using the Simplified Menopausal Index, including vasomotor, psychological, and somatic domains, with higher scores indicating greater symptom burden. Results: Among 79 participants, 43 reported poor sleep quality and 36 reported good sleep quality. Women with poor sleep quality had higher total and domain-specific SMI scores and shorter objective sleep duration. In logistic regression analyses adjusted for age and objective sleep duration, total SMI score and each symptom domain were associated with poor sleep quality. These associations remained significant in sensitivity analyses excluding the sleep-related SMI item from the total score and psychological domain score. Conclusions: Self-reported poor sleep quality among Japanese working women aged 40 years and older may reflect menopausal symptom burden beyond objectively measured sleep duration. The consistency of the findings across sensitivity analyses supports the robustness of this association. Sleep complaints may therefore serve as an accessible signal for recognizing menopausal symptom burden in clinical and occupational health settings.

items.title: Migraine and related burden among employees of participating enterprises in China: a cross-sectional study
items.abstract: Migraine imposes a substantial burden on working-age populations, but evidence on migraine burden of industry category among enterprise employees remains limited. This study aimed to describe the proportion of employees meeting migraine criteria and migraine-related burden in a convenience sample of participating enterprises, and to explore their associations with industry category and measured work- and sleep-related characteristics. This cross-sectional study included 10,592 full-time employees, recruited from participating enterprises across 19 industry categories using multistage convenience sampling. Migraine was identified using the HARDSHIP questionnaire and clinical assessment according to ICHD-3 criteria. Sociodemographic factors, industry category, work schedule, sleep-related factors, migraine characteristics, disability, productivity loss, healthcare use, economic burden, coping behaviors, and social support were analyzed. Multivariable logistic regression was used to assess factors associated with migraine. Among 10,592 employees, 2,792 participants met the study criteria for migraine, corresponding to an observed proportion of 26.36% in the analytic sample. The observed proportions differed across industry categories represented by the participating enterprises. Industry group was associated with migraine status after adjustment for the prespecified covariates. Insomnia frequency and later bedtime were consistently associated with higher observed migraine proportions across work-schedule groups, whereas patterns for night-shift frequency and working hours varied by work schedule. Participants with migraine reported substantial productivity loss, including reduced work efficiency, night-shift interruption, cancelled work-related activities, and limitations in family activities. Psychological distress, coping behaviors, and perceived social support also differed across industry category. Migraine represents an important occupational health concern among employees of participating enterprises, with its observed distribution and burden varying across occupational and work-schedule contexts. Workplace programs should integrate migraine recognition, access to care, sleep-health promotion, and appropriate scheduling accommodations. Prospective representative studies with detailed occupational exposures and clinical covariates are needed to confirm these associations and evaluate targeted interventions.

items.title: Morphological Characteristics and the Location-Dependent Variations of Thumb–Touchscreen Contact Areas in Two-Thumb Mobile Interaction
items.abstract: This study quantitatively investigated morphological characteristics of traces occurring between thumbs and touchscreen during two-thumb touch interaction on a mobile device. Thirty-two college students were recruited, and a paper-and-ink-based touch simulation using a mockup was conducted to capture thumb touch traces. Traces were collected at 22 target points on the virtual keyboard region, encompassing flexion–extension and abduction–adduction thumb movements, and the location-dependent variations in morphology were analyzed using major axis orientation, eccentricity, and area size (elliptical features). Results exhibited that during thumb displacement from flexion to extension, the major axes of the traces rotated clockwise for the left thumb and counterclockwise for the right, while the traces themselves became more circular and increased in size. In addition, during thumb excursion from abduction to adduction, the major axes of the traces generally rotated clockwise for the left thumb and counterclockwise for the right, while the traces became more elongated and showed no statistically significant change in area.

items.title: MOTIVATIONAL STRATEGIES OF SCIENCE TEACHERS AND STUDENT GRADE PERFORMANCE BASIS FOR INTERVENTION PROGRAM
items.abstract: The motivational strategies used by Science teachers and their relationship with students’ engagement and academic performance were assessed in this study as a basis for an intervention program. The study was conducted from June to November 2025. It examined teachers' use of intrinsic and extrinsic motivational strategies, students' behavioral, emotional, and cognitive engagement, their academic performance in Science, and their relationships. Quantitative descriptive-correlational research was conducted to 147 Grade 7 learners. Validated survey questionnaires and academic grade performance in Science were utilized to collect data. Descriptive statistics, such as the weighted mean and standard deviation, were used to characterize the variables, while Spearman’s rho was used to assess relationships among motivational strategies, student engagement, and academic grade performance. The results indicated that science teachers actively used extrinsic and intrinsic motivational strategies. Most students demonstrated behavioral, emotional, and cognitive engagement, and their first-quarter performance in Science showed strong academic competence. Furthermore, the intrinsic and extrinsic motivational strategies had a weak positive, statistically significant link with grade performance. However, no significant association was identified between the motivational strategies and students' behavioral, emotional, or cognitive engagement. The study indicates that motivational strategies have some impact on students’ academic performance, but the effect is very limited. The study led to the development of the Science Motivation and Engagement Enhancement Program (SMEEP) as an intervention to improve students’ motivation, engagement, and academic achievement in Science. The program involves intrinsic and extrinsic motivational strategies through well-organized pre-assessment, implementation, and post-assessment activities.

items.title: Multimodal Evaluation of Exoskeleton Assistance Using Optimized Machine Learning
items.abstract: Repetitive manual material handling (MMH) remains a leading occupational risk factor for work-related musculoskeletal disorders (WMSD), and passive shoulder-support exoskeletons have emerged as promising assistive technologies. Most evaluations rely on group-level statistics from single sensor modalities, leaving open whether their effects can be detected at the individual level. Thirty-five adults performed low-risk (4.54 kg, Lift Index (LI) < 1.0) lifting tasks, derived from the Revised NIOSH Lifting Equation, with and without the passive shoulder exoskeleton support. Surface electromyography (sEMG), inertial measurement unit (IMU) kinematics, and NASA Task Load Index (NASA-TLX) ratings were derived into a 34 feature vector and classified using four models under Leave-One-Subject-Out Cross Validation to ensure our models were not trained on already seen data. SVM with radial basis kernel reached 89.4% accuracy (AUC = 0.932) on low-risk lifting, Logistic Regression reached 84.8% (AUC = 0.904) on high-risk lifting. NASATLX physical demand proved to be the most important feature in permutation importance, outranking all biomechanical features. Perceived workload may be a more consistent cross-subject signal than objective biomechanics, with practical implications for low-burden field evaluation.

items.title: Non-Linear Analysis and Optimization of Weight and Center of Mass for AR Glasses Wear Comfort
items.abstract: This article investigates the effects of weight and Center of Mass (CoM) of AR glasses on subjective assessment during wearing tasks. Utilizing a modular prototyping system, 100 participants evaluated 20 weight-CoM configurations. To address the limitations of linearized Likert scale data, this study constructed a hybrid analytical framework incorporating Generalized Estimating Equations, Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) with SHAP explanations, and Polynomial Response Surface Methodology. The results revealed significant non-linear coupling effects of weight and CoM on comfort and established a quantitative engineering mapping model based on ordinal data analysis. Furthermore, SHAP analysis identified dynamic stability and nasal comfort as the two most influential perceptual dimensions, jointly accounting for 79.2% of the total SHAP importance. Accordingly, this study proposes engineering optimization guidelines for AR glasses, providing a quantitative basis for lightweighting and weight-distribution optimization of wearable devices.

items.title: Occupational Hazards Associated with Pig Production in Southern Senatorial District of Cross River State, Nigeria
items.abstract: The study examined occupational hazards common among pig farmers and workers in the Southern Senatorial District of Cross River State, Nigeria. The research was guided with four research purposes and questions, and three hypotheses. Survey design was adopted and farm owners, workers and farm owners’ families constituted the population for the study. A sample of hundred and twenty (120) respondents was drawn from the seven local government areas that formed the study area, and were administered questionnaire items. Data collected were analyzed using descriptive statistics and inferential analyses, including chi-squares tests and independent sample t-tests at 0.05 level of significance. The result revealed the socioeconomic characteristics, common associated hazards and health problems experience by the respondents. Economically exposed respondents lost greatly more income due to illness less than their non-exposed counterparts (t = 5.87, p<0.05). Significantly safety training was greatly associated with Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) usage (𝑥2 =21.54, p<0.05). The study concludes that pig production in the study area poses substantial occupational health and economic risks. The research recommends among others regular training on safety and zoonosis prevention, sensitization of farmers on safe handling practices and farm hygiene, enaction of policies supporting occupational health surveillance, and establishment of rural health clinics and mobile health outreach for pig farmers.

items.title: Occupational Health, Safety and Environmental Compliance and its Effects: A Case Study of Federal Polytechnic Bauchi, Nigeria
items.abstract: Occupational Health, Safety and Environmental (OHSE) compliance is a dynamic requirement for ensuring wellbeing, safety at work environments, curtailing work-related hazards and reassuring sustainable institutional procedures. This research evaluates the quality of OHSE compliance and its effects at Federal Polytechnic Bauchi, Nigeria. The study method adopted a cast study involving structured questionnaires, workplace adherences and inspection of safety-related documents. The study emphasized on safety observances, hazard regulatory procedures, personal protective equipment accessibility, emergency enthusiasm and environmental management routines. The findings demonstrate that effective OHSE compliance contributes significantly to accident prevention, better productivity, environmental safety and enhanced institutional sustainability. However, problems such as inadequate safety mindfulness, incoherent monitoring, inadequate safety resources and weak enforcement methods negate full compliance. The research recommends continuous safety training, enhanced inspection protocols, adequate provision of safety facilities (PPE), better-quality waste control systems and stronger institutional OHSE policies to intensify workshop safety and routine.

items.title: Operational and organizational training for managing work stress among police investigation officers: a global perspective
items.abstract: Criminal investigators face chronic demands beyond general police work: repeated analysis of traumatic digital evidence, heavy caseloads, cognitive overload, evidentiary scrutiny, and accountability for error (Schlosser et al., 2024;Strickland et al., 2023;Woodhams and Duran, 2024).Digitalization and rapidly changing technical requirements intensify these pressures while recruitment and retention problems restrict capacity (Drew et al., 2024). Burnout consequently threatens both officer well-being and investigative quality (Bezie et al., 2024).The literature separates operational stressors, which are intrinsic to the work, from organizational stressors, which arise from how the institution is run, such as workload allocation, supervisory support, role clarity, and culture (Gavin and Porter, 2024). A finding that is decisive for training design is that organizational and operational stressors, rather than trauma exposure alone, predict most stressrelated outcomes among investigative and forensic staff (Keech and Drew, 2026;Porter and Gavin, 2025). Among United States investigators exposed to CSAM, the frequency of exposure was not systematically related to mental health, apart from violent material, which was linked to elevated posttraumatic stress; agency-level factors such as control over workload, debriefing, and feedback on case outcomes were what mitigated harm (Mitchell et al., 2023). This Opinion draws on peer-reviewed studies published between 2022 and 2026, identified through database searches on police and investigator occupational stress, psychological capital, technostress, and organizational interventions, prioritizing evidence specific to investigative and forensic roles and using the broader occupational-health literature where role-specific studies are scarce. On that basis, I argue that stress-management interventions for investigators should rest on two complementary pillars. Operational training strengthens the adaptive capacity of the individual officer; organizational training reshapes the leadership, climate, and work systems in which officers operate (Figure 1). Current practice still leans heavily toward the first pillar, locating both the problem and its remedy in the worker. I treat investigator resilience as a structurally enabled resource rather than a fixed personal trait. The evidence supports a structural rather than an episodic framing. Multidimensional assessments show that police stress tracks enduring features of the work environment, including job demands, control, support, role clarity, and organizational change, more than isolated critical incidents (Strukcinskiene et al., 2025). Within investigative and forensic units, organizational and operational demands, not trauma exposure alone, predict the largest share of stress-related outcomes, while supervisor support, peer support, and a positive psychosocial safety climate act as the main buffering resources (Keech and Drew, 2026). This pattern recasts exposure as one demand among several rather than the sole cause of harm (Drew et al., 2024).The job demands-resources (JD-R) model explains how demands deplete well-being unless balanced by resources. Conservation of resources (COR) theory explains how continued depletion without recovery creates loss spirals and burnout (Demerouti et al., 2001;Hobfoll, 1989;Zhou et al., 2024). Operational training adds personal resources; organizational action protects them.Integration requires a multilevel and temporal account. Structural demands such as backlog, traumatic exposure, digital overload and ambiguity first activate the JD-R health-impairment pathway. The two pillars then operate in a reciprocal cycle: operational training may improve immediate regulation, appraisal and help-seeking, while organizational training changes workload, supervisory behaviour, recovery opportunities and psychological safety. These organizational changes determine whether personal gains are replenished or progressively depleted. COR theory therefore predicts that operational training is most useful during acute demand, whereas organizational redesign becomes increasingly important when demands are recurrent, controllable and system-generated. Professional identity is proposed as a mediator, not a presumed protection: stress may weaken identification through cynicism and perceived value conflict, while credible supervision and meaningful feedback may restore identification and its wellbeing benefits. Job security is proposed as a moderator because officers who fear transfer, stigma, career penalty or job loss may be less able to disclose strain or use support. The model predicts that combined interventions will be more durable when workload control, psychological safety and leadership accountability improve; it does not assume that combined interventions will always outperform individual training.Digital transformation adds a further, persistent demand. Technostress, the strain from constant connectivity, information overload, and the intrusion of technology into recovery time, behaves as a chronic job demand associated with lower well-being and burnout, and it is intrinsic to investigative work built around digital evidence (Pansini et al., 2023;Mansuroğlu and Smith, 2026). Two resources deserve emphasis because they locate where interventions should act. Professional identity mediates the link between occupational stress and well-being, and perceived job security moderates it, which indicates that meaning and stability are protective resources shaped largely by organizations rather than by individuals alone (Wu et al., 2025).Operational training targets the officer's own coping repertoire and has a credible evidence base.Mindfulness-based resilience training has shown feasibility and promising effects on stress in police samples (Christopher et al., 2024), and physiologically grounded programs that pair heart-ratevariability biofeedback with metacognitive skill practice are being trialed to build resilience in officers exposed to post-traumatic stress injuries (Andersen et al., 2023). These approaches develop psychological capital, the malleable resources of hope, efficacy, resilience, and optimism that are associated with lower burnout and turnover intention and with higher engagement and performance (Loghman et al., 2023).The limits of a purely individual approach are equally clear, and they should be stated without overclaiming the alternative. Worker-directed interventions place the burden of adaptation on the person, can imply that distress signals personal weakness, and tend to fade once officers return to unchanged conditions. They do not remediate the organizational stressors that the investigatorspecific evidence identifies as the deepest sources of harm (Gavin and Porter, 2024;Mitchell et al., 2023). Teaching investigators to regulate their physiology is useful, but it does not reduce an unmanageable caseload or a dismissive command climate.Comparative reviews suggest that organizational and combined interventions may produce benefits comparable with, and sometimes more durable than, individual interventions in healthcare and general workplaces (Catapano et al., 2023;Dahlqvist et al., 2023). This evidence cannot be treated as direct proof for investigative policing. Its relevance is theoretical and conditional: reducing demands at source should protect recovery, but policing adds hierarchy, operational urgency, confidentiality requirements and occupational stigma. Accordingly, the present framework offers a testable proposition rather than an effectiveness claim. Organizational action should be staged according to readiness, fidelity, leadership commitment and resources, with individual training retained as an accessible component while system-level effects are evaluated.For investigative units, this pillar includes trauma-informed supervision, case-outcome feedback, exposure and caseload review, breaks and recovery after graphic-material work, peer support, psychosocial safety monitoring, and leadership accountability (Mitchell et al., 2022(Mitchell et al., , 2023;;Keech and Drew, 2026). Leadership links the pillars because supportive leadership can strengthen psychological capital (Loghman et al., 2023). Table 1 distinguishes evidence from proposals requiring testing.Delivery should fit agency capacity. National laboratories may use exposure logging, specialist supervision, and rotation; small or rural forces may need regional case-sharing, remote consultation, peer supervision, and referral agreements. Internet-crime task forces may prioritize graphicexposure limits and outcome feedback, while general detective units address backlog, autonomy, and recovery. In lower-resource settings, feasible minimums include workload review, supervisor training, confidential referral, and protected recovery. The functions are transferable, but implementation must reflect staffing, geography, labor protections, culture, and stigma.Implementation barriers require active design responses. Hierarchy can be addressed through confidential reporting routes, supervisor accountability and protected escalation pathways; resource constraints through phased implementation and regional/shared services; stigma through routine, universal wellbeing processes rather than exceptional referral; confidentiality concerns through independent providers and clear data-governance rules; and competing priorities through integrating recovery, exposure review and case-outcome feedback into existing quality and supervision meetings.These strategies are proposed implementation mechanisms, not evidence of established effectiveness. Access to resilience resources may vary by gender, rank, rurality, contract status, unit type and national capacity (Bezie et al., 2024;Porter and Gavin, 2025). Women officers may encounter additional caregiving demands, gendered expectations or lower psychological safety; junior officers may have less discretion to request recovery; rural officers may face distance, limited specialist services and confidentiality concerns in small teams. These conditions may alter both exposure to demands and the feasibility of each intervention. Implementation should therefore require disaggregated monitoring of reach, uptake, workload relief, perceived safety and outcomes by gender, rank, rurality and unit. Agencies should offer multiple access routes, remote and regional options, protected time, culturally appropriate providers and safeguards against career penalties. Core functions should be retained, but delivery should be adapted and tested rather than assumed to be equivalent across contexts.The pillars are complementary but not interchangeable. Policy should become auditable and equitable. Units should review caseload and graphic exposure regularly; provide confidential, trauma-informed supervision; record access to case-outcome feedback; protect recovery; and monitor climate, absence, turnover intention and support uptake. Universal exposure caps are premature. Agencies should instead define local trigger points for mandatory workload review, document exceptions and test whether thresholds predict health and service outcomes. Senior leaders should be accountable for system indicators alongside case throughput. Every implementation should report reach and effects by gender, rank, rurality, unit type and national context, and should include safeguards against retaliation, disclosure of sensitive case information and unequal access. items.title: Organizational Performance as A Systemic Construct
items.abstract: This study reconceptualizes organizational performance through the lens of systems thinking, arguing that conventional financial and efficiency-based approaches are increasingly inadequate for capturing the complexity of contemporary organizations. In response, this study develops a systemic conceptualization of performance as a multidimensional and emergent construct. Drawing on classical and contemporary contributions to systems theory, the analysis conceptualizes the organization as a complex sociotechnical system composed of interdependent subsystems embedded within dynamic environments. Within this framework, performance is not treated as a static outcome but as a dynamic property emerging from continuous interactions between internal structures and external conditions. This article examines the evolution of performance theories, from traditional financial models to multidimensional frameworks such as the Competing Values Framework, and discusses contemporary measurement approaches, including the Balanced Scorecard and sustainability-oriented frameworks. It ultimately proposes a systemic conception of performance structured around a viability-performance matrix, emphasizing feedback loops, adaptive capacity, and structural tensions between stability and flexibility. This study contributes to management theory by bridging systems thinking and performance literature, with implications for organizational design, governance, and sustainability-oriented management.

items.title: Parameter Identification and Situation Awareness in Distribution Networks Under Incomplete Information Driven by Data-Physical Fusion
items.abstract: Some distribution networks are characterized by weak grid structures and complex feeder deployment, which leads to missing information such as line parameters. Existing power flow methods depend heavily on accurate parameters and lack sufficient dynamic adaptability, making them unsuitable for incomplete-information conditions. To address this problem, this paper proposes a distribution-network situation-awareness model driven by data-physical fusion. First, to cope with the dual challenges of incompleteness and uncertainty in line parameters, a bounded multi-operating-condition line-parameter identification model is constructed, and the covariance matrix adaptation evolution strategy is employed to determine line resistances and reactances; the resulting parameters are then used for data augmentation. Next, a situation-awareness model for distribution networks is developed by combining a physics-informed neural network with a mixture-of-experts architecture. In this way, data-driven learning is integrated with physical constraints so that the perceptual capability of deep learning is preserved while the model remains guided by power-flow physics. Finally, the model is validated using the IEEE 33-bus system and historical operating data from an actual distribution area in China. The results show that the proposed model outperforms the comparison methods on the IEEE 33-bus system and effectively tracks multiple state variables in the actual distribution area, supporting its feasibility for incomplete-information conditions.

items.title: Physical and Psychosocial Occupational Hazards Among Solid Waste Collectors in Swali Yenagoa, Bayelsa State
items.abstract: Proper solid waste disposal is vital for public and environmental health, and waste collectors play a central role in maintaining community sanitation. Solid waste collectors experience high rates of injuries such as cuts and musculoskeletal disorders in Africa, largely due to inadequate PPE, poor training, and limited healthcare access. This study is significant because it fills the gap in community-level data on physical and psychosocial occupational hazards among solid waste collectors in Swali, Yenagoa, and providing evidence to improve occupational health and safety practices. The aim of this study was to assess the physical and psychosocial occupational hazards among waste collectors in Swali Community, Yenagoa, Bayelsa State. This research adopted a cross-sectional survey design. The target population comprised of all formal waste collectors in the Swali community who were exposed to physical and psychosocial occupational hazards. A total of 125 waste collectors were selected using a simple random sampling technique. Data was collected through structured questionnaire and observational checklist over a period of seven (7) weeks and analyzed using descriptive statistics with the aid of SPSS version 25. Findings revealed that the most frequently reported physical occupational hazard was cuts or puncture wounds with 44.8% of respondents agreeing and 24.0% strongly agreeing, yielding the highest mean score of 3.67 ± 1.18. Regarding psychosocial hazards, 52% reported experiencing stress due to your job, while 51% reported verbal abuse while working. In conclusion, the study found that waste collectors in Swali, Yenagoa, experience significant physical and psychosocial hazards. It is recommended that PPE compliance policies should be enforced and provision of safe work technique.

items.title: Play-Based Approach: A Strategy in Teaching Number Recognition Among Kindergarteners in Private School
items.abstract: This study examined the effectiveness of a play-centered approach in teaching number recognition among kindergarten learners of Inter-Asia Business Institute Philippines Incorporated during the School Year 2025–2026. Guided by the theories of Vygotsky, Dewey, and Montessori, the research utilized a one-group pretest-posttest design involving fifteen (15) kindergarten learners. The intervention integrated play-based activities such as number games, counting hopscotch, and storytelling to enhance cognitive engagement and numeracy skills. Findings revealed a significant improvement in learners’ posttest scores compared to their pretest performance, as confirmed by the Wilcoxon Signed-Rank Test (p < 0.001). The results indicated that the play-based approach effectively enhanced learners’ number recognition, motivation, and class participation. The study concluded that play-based learning is a powerful instructional method that fosters holistic child development and supports the MATATAG curriculum’s goals of meaningful and enjoyable learning. It recommended broader adoption of play-centered strategies in early childhood education to strengthen foundational numeracy skills.

items.title: Post-wildfire reforestation in Canada: Practitioner perspectives, emerging practices, and future research needs
items.abstract: Wildfire research and management efforts have largely focused on fire suppression, risk assessment, and mitigation. Comparatively little attention has been given to post-wildfire reforestation, despite its potential influence on long-term forest recovery. To better understand post-wildfire restoration practices in Canada, national charity Forests Canada conducted a survey resulting in 80 responses from forest managers and tree planting practitioners. Forests Canada also conducted interviews with eight experts. The study examined decision-making processes guiding post-fire tree planting, operational practices used to promote successful forest establishment, and the extent to which future wildfire risk is considered during restoration planning. Results indicate that practitioners generally adopt a cautious and deliberate approach to post-wildfire reforestation. Key considerations include regeneration assessments, resource availability, regulatory requirements, environmental and wildlife values, community priorities, and site accessibility. Respondents reported several adjustments to traditional reforestation practices, particularly regarding tree spacing, microsite selection, operational costs, occupational health and safety measures, and consideration of future fire risk. Changes in species selection, nursery stock types, and salvage logging practices were also reported, although less consistently. The study identifies seven priority knowledge gaps requiring further attention: reforestation prioritization, species selection, Indigenous stewardship pathways, tree planting standards, site preparation and salvage logging, the true costs of artificial regeneration, and occupational health and safety.

items.title: Potential for real-time health and welfare monitoring of red fox (Vulpes vulpes) in experimental settings using implants
items.abstract: Monitoring and improving animal health and welfare is a pressing need. Technological advances are increasing our ability to do so in a range of settings but there are limited uses in experimental settings for less common model animals. Red foxes ( Vulpes vulpes ) are maintained by the French National Agency for Food, Environmental, and Occupational Health and Safety (ANSES) for regulatory and research purposes, primarily related to its role as a European Union and French Reference Laboratory for rabies and Echinococcus spp., both serious zoonoses. In 2022, four foxes were surgically fitted with internal implants that recorded body temperature and activity levels and subsequently inoculated with rabies virus (RABV). As a proof of concept, we retrospectively tested the potential of these two variables to provide an early warning for the onset of rabies symptoms. To do so, we applied two anomaly detection algorithms (Shewhart and EWMA) with varying confidence levels individually to the two data sets from each fox and compared how early the different models could detect significant changes while limiting false alarms during the calibration period. We found that all the foxes significantly changed their activity during infection. We were best able to detect these changes at the individual fox level using the EWMA algorithm, in some cases producing consecutive alarms up to two weeks before the death of an animal, while limiting false alarms. We found no evidence of fever in any of the infected foxes and body temperature did not appear to be a reliable indicator of foxes’ health in this context. While here we applied our methods to a particularly severe and rarely implemented model with a limited sample size, this proof of concept illustrates the potential of these methods for a wide range of other situations that would benefit from similar long-term monitoring, including experimental protocols with milder clinical signs and routine monitoring for unexpected declines in health or welfare.

items.title: Prevalence of night work in the Brazilian employed population.
items.abstract: Introduction: Night work and extended work schedules are among the leading occupational health risk factors. Objectives: To estimate the prevalence of night work among the employed Brazilian population. Methods: Cross-sectional, population-based study using data from the 2019 Brazilian National Survey of Health. Individuals aged 15 years or older who belonged to the economically active employed population were included. The outcome was self-reported night work, assessed using a survey question on work performed between 8:00 p.m. and 5:00 a.m. Responses were recorded as 0 = no and 1 = yes. Prevalence estimates and their 95% CIs were calculated accounting for the complex survey design according to sociodemographic, occupational, and state-level characteristics. Associations were evaluated using the Rao-Scott adjusted Pearson chi-square test. Results: The national prevalence of night work was 13.3% (95% CI, 12.8%-13.9%), ranging from 5.8% in Acre to 16.6% in Rio de Janeiro. Night work was more frequent in urban areas (14.2%), among men (16.3%), and among higher-income individuals (15.5%). The highest prevalences were observed in the accommodation and food services (28.7%) and transportation, warehousing, and postal services (26.9%) sectors. Conclusions: Approximately one in seven workers in Brazil engaged in night work. The prevalence varied according to regional, sociodemographic, and occupational characteristics, with higher prevalences in sectors requiring continuous operations. These findings underscore the importance of monitoring work schedules and implementing policies to protect the health of workers exposed to night work.

items.title: Recent Developments in Global Probabilistic Turbulence Forecast Products for Aeronautical Meteorology at Deutscher Wetterdienst
items.abstract: Atmospheric turbulence is a major hazard for commercial flight operations. As a result, reliable and easily interpretable meteorological forecast data for this hazard is paramount to the safety of aircraft, crew and passengers. To meet this requirement, Deutscher Wetterdienst (DWD) has further improved their forecast products by blending the traditional deterministic numerical weather prediction of the Eddy-Dissipation-Parameter (EDP) with the probabilistic forecast to exceed the severe turbulence threshold of the EDP from its operational ensemble prediction system (EPS). Building on those results and inspired by an agile co-design approach with key users, a turbulence advisory was conceived which condenses three-dimensional spatial information into two dimensions in order to further support situational awareness and complement traditional aeronautical meteorological charts. In this technical note, the necessity for products of this kind is motivated and their design and specifications are briefly explained.

items.title: RecToolBench: Benchmarking Recommendation-Specific Tool Orchestration under Fuzzy User Intent
items.abstract: Recent advances in agentic recommender systems are shifting recommender systems from passive filtering engines to instruction-following agents that use external tools to resolve user intent. However, existing benchmarks often assume explicit user intent, simplified tool environments, or isolated function calls, leaving realistic tool orchestration for recommendation underexplored. To bridge this gap, we propose RecToolBench, a Model Context Protocol (MCP)-based benchmark for evaluating tool-using recommender agents under fuzzy user instructions. RecToolBench contains more than 1,200 executable tasks across three recommendation domains, 13 MCP servers, and 32 tools, spanning single-tool calls, parallel tool calls, sequential tool chains, and hybrid tool orchestration. We construct RecToolBench with a scalable synthesize--fuzzify--judge pipeline that generates executable fuzzy recommendation tasks, and evaluates agent trajectories using rule-based execution checks and rubric-based LLM evaluation. Experiments on representative LLMs show that syntactically valid tool calls do not guarantee successful recommendations. Models struggle with semantic parameter grounding, multi-step evidence integration, and grounded final recommendations, especially as orchestration complexity increases. Our results identify tool orchestration under fuzzy user intent as a major bottleneck for agentic recommender systems. Our data and code are available at https://github.com/ShawnChenn/RecToolBench.

items.title: Redefining healthcare roles in the age of AI: a sociotechnical perspective on professional adaptation and training
items.abstract: Purpose This study investigates the impact of artificial intelligence (AI) implementation on healthcare professional role adaptation and training program effectiveness, examining the mediating roles of sociotechnical integration and professional attitudes towards AI. Design/methodology/approach A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 255 healthcare professionals in India, including physicians, nurses, paramedical, and support staff from various facility types. The study employed a quantitative approach using validated scales to measure AI Technology Implementation, Sociotechnical Integration, Professional Attitudes towards AI, Professional Role Adaptation, and Training Program Effectiveness. Findings AI implementation had significant positive total effects on both professional role adaptation and training program effectiveness. These effects were partially mediated by sociotechnical integration and professional attitudes towards AI: both mediators transmitted a significant positive indirect effect from AI implementation to each outcome, while the direct effects remained positive and significant. Sociotechnical integration was the stronger mediator, particularly for training program effectiveness. The effects varied across different healthcare roles and facility types. Practical implications The findings emphasize the need for healthcare organizations to foster positive attitudes towards AI among staff, ensure thorough sociotechnical integration, and develop tailored, context-sensitive approaches to AI implementation and training programs. Originality/value This study provides a detailed, empirically grounded account of AI adoption in healthcare, showing that the benefits of AI implementation for professional roles and training are channelled through social and organizational factors rather than arising from technology alone. It highlights the critical importance of human factors and organizational context in shaping AI implementation outcomes, contributing to a more nuanced understanding of technological change in healthcare settings.

items.title: Reflecting on 35 Years of the Office Ergonomics Research Committee (OERC): Funded Research to Reality Studies
items.abstract: The Office Ergonomics Research Committee (OERC) is an industry research consortium consisting of companies that collaborate to advance ergonomics/human factors research in the design and management of knowledge workplaces, systems, processes, and products. OERC members represent a diverse group of organizations with a common interest in complex human-computer technology systems, namely, office ergonomics. Members of OERC seek to expand their understanding of the human-technology system in office settings through sponsored research by partnering with university researchers to advance knowledge in human factors/ergonomics. OERC has funded research projects that explore novel approaches, address underexplored challenges, and generate research with actionable insights that support healthier, more productive, and equitable office environments for over 35 years. This panel comprises OERC members and previously OERC-funded university researchers, who will present highlights and reflections on their academic research projects as well as the benefits and roles of OERC membership.

items.title: Responsive Digital Pedagogy for Elementary Learner Engagement
items.abstract: This study explored the predictive role of responsive digital pedagogy in shaping elementary learner engagement in Baggao, Cagayan. It focused on four dimensions of digital teaching: adaptive digital task design, responsive feedback, participatory digital interaction, and access-sensitive instructional support. An explanatory-predictive path design was applied to data from 90 public elementary school teachers selected through stratified criterion-random sampling. Responses were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling, bootstrapping with 10,000 resamples, PLSpredict, and importance-performance map analysis. The measurement model established acceptable reliability, convergent validity, and discriminant validity. Results showed that responsive digital pedagogy explained 62.4% of the variance in learner engagement. Responsive feedback exerted the strongest positive effect, followed by participatory digital interaction and adaptive digital task design. Access-sensitive instructional support, however, did not significantly predict engagement and emerged as the weakest area of implementation. Predictive analysis further showed that the model performed better in explaining active participation, sustained attention, and learning effort than cognitive involvement. These findings suggest that the effectiveness of digital instruction depends less on technology use itself and more on how teachers adapt digital experiences, provide timely feedback, and create meaningful opportunities for participation. Strengthening access-sensitive practices and designing tasks that promote deeper cognitive engagement are recommended to improve responsive digital teaching in elementary classrooms.

items.title: Robotic surgery in Italian hospitals
items.abstract: Robotic-assisted surgery has become an increasingly established component of contemporary hospital practice, yet its integration into healthcare systems remains heterogeneous and often shaped by local resources, institutional ambition, reimbursement constraints, and variable governance models. The current debate should therefore move beyond the binary question of whether robotic surgery is superior to laparoscopy or open surgery, and should instead address how robotic programs can be implemented, monitored, financed, and governed responsibly within real hospital systems. This Associazione Chirurghi Ospedalieri Italiani position paper proposes a practical framework for the value-based governance of robotic surgery in Italian hospitals. The document does not advocate unrestricted technological expansion, nor does it interpret robotic surgery as intrinsically superior across all procedures. Rather, it argues that robotic-assisted surgery should be considered a high-complexity surgical program requiring defined indications, institutional competence, procedural volume, structured training, credentialing, team-based preparation, prospective outcome monitoring, registry participation, and periodic reassessment. The article emphasizes that the value of robotic surgery cannot be evaluated solely through acquisition costs, operative time, or isolated perioperative endpoints. Conversion avoidance, access to complex minimally invasive surgery, technical reproducibility, patient selection, length of stay, postoperative recovery, training scalability, surgeon ergonomics, operating room organization, and digital readiness should be considered within a broader health-system perspective. At the same time, economic sustainability requires value-based procurement, appropriate reimbursement models, avoidance of low-volume fragmentation, and transparent accountability. Associazione Chirurghi Ospedalieri Italiani supports a governance model in which robotic surgery is clinically appropriate, institutionally mature, economically sustainable, continuously monitored, and equitably accessible. The future of robotic surgery in Italian hospitals will depend not only on technological availability, but on the capacity of surgeons, managers, regional authorities, payers, and policy-makers to align innovation with evidence, accountability, equity, and measurable patient-centered value.

items.title: Sampling Safe Futures: Multimodal Trajectory Planning for Personalized Safety in Anthropomorphic AI
items.abstract: Anthropomorphic artificial intelligence systems increasingly remember personal details, display empathy, and are engaged with as social counterparts, creating forms of risk that emerge from the evolution of the user-system relationship over time. Existing safeguards largely operate at the level of individual conversational turns and cannot determine whether a sequence of seemingly acceptable interactions is cumulatively moving a particular user toward harm. This paper introduces personalized trajectory-level safety, a framework that treats relational safety as a sequential decision problem over a latent escalation state inferred from the user's messages and influenced by the system's responses. At each turn, a screening step first discards any response strategy that does not preserve at least one safe continuation of the interaction under every plausible model of the user. Among the remaining strategies, we formulate action selection as multimodal trajectory sampling, and use a Generative Flow Network to generate diverse future evolutions in proportion to their plausibility, safety, and utility. The system then selects the strategy that preserves the largest fraction of safe and useful continuations. We evaluate the framework in simulation, calibrated on statistics reported for real human-chatbot interactions, and using response strategies derived from public benchmarks. Results show that trajectory-aware decision making substantially reduces the frequency of harmful states while keeping helpful interaction. This work reframes safety for anthropomorphic AI from response-level filtering to personalized control over the future evolution of human-AI relationships. The source code is available at https://github.com/benedettapicano/ANTHROPOMORPHIC_SAFETY_TRAJ.

items.title: Self-Supervised Representation Learning: From Spectral Foundation Models to Auroral Emission Spectra
items.abstract: Auroral spectrographs such as the Auroral Spectrograph In Skibotn (ASIS) record hundreds of thousands of emission spectra, but only a few hundred can be labelled by an expert. To exploit the rest, we pretrain a 1D Vision Transformer with a masked autoencoder on 223,000 unlabelled spectra. Without labels, its representation recovers the emission-line intensity ratios that physicists use to diagnose the precipitating particles (R^2 0.91 vs. 0.77 for an untrained control) and, under one linear probe, classifies as well as 13 features designed by experts. Fine-tuned, the model outperforms the previous supervised auroral classifier on its own benchmark (macro-AP 88.5 vs. 77.8), reaches 0.870 mAP, and exceeds the same architecture trained from scratch by +0.159 with 10% of the labels; attribution shows that it uses both N2+ bands. Could an existing pretrained model replace it? Two astronomical spectral foundation models and a time-series model transfer according to their spectral window: SpectraFM, trained in the infrared, falls below the untrained control, whereas SpecFormer, trained in the optical, approaches in-domain pretraining without reaching it.

items.title: Ship navigation behavior pattern mining: Representations and intelligent methods
items.abstract: Summary: Maritime transportation is a core pillar of global trade. Mining meaningful behavioral patterns from ship trajectories is essential for characterizing ship movement regularities, supporting maritime traffic management, and improving maritime situational awareness. Although substantial progress has been made in anomaly detection, trajectory prediction, and scenario-specific behavior recognition, publicly available labeled datasets remain limited by incomplete labeling schemes, and ship behavior modeling still lacks a unified framework. To clarify these gaps, this review systematically examines data sources, labeled datasets, behavior modeling, mining methods, and practical applications related to ship navigation behavior pattern mining. It further proposes a three-layer behavior modeling framework that organizes ship behavior into physical behavior, interactive behavior, and semantic behavior. This framework connects low-level motion states, spatiotemporal interactions with the maritime environment and other ships, and high-level semantic interpretation, thereby providing a structured basis for understanding behavioral patterns in ship trajectories. Building on this review, we summarize the major challenges and future research directions in the field. This study provides a reference for subsequent research and aims to promote the development of ship navigation behavior pattern mining, particularly by extending spatial data mining methods for static data toward spatiotemporal pattern mining of dynamic streaming data from moving objects.

items.title: Situational Awareness as a Human Factor in Near Miss and Crash Incidents Among Student Motorcyclists
items.abstract: Motorcycle riders are among the most vulnerable road users due to their direct exposure to dynamic traffic environments, while many traffic accidents are preceded by near-miss incidents that provide valuable opportunities for proactive safety evaluation. This study aimed to examine the effect of Situational Awareness (SA) on near-miss and crash incidents among university student motorcycle riders and to evaluate the contribution of the Situation Awareness Rating Technique (SART) dimensions, namely Demand, Supply, and Understanding. A quantitative cross-sectional design was employed involving 96 Universitas Malikussaleh students selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire based on the SART instrument and analyzed using simple and multiple linear regression after confirming the validity and reliability of the instrument and the fulfillment of regression assumptions. The results demonstrated that Situational Awareness had a significant negative effect on both near-miss (β = −0.614, p < 0.001) and crash incidents (β = −0.370, p < 0.001), explaining 48.7% and 42.3% of the variance, respectively. Furthermore, the Understanding dimension consistently showed the strongest influence on both safety outcomes, whereas the Supply dimension was not significantly associated with crash incidents. These findings indicate that improving riders' cognitive ability to recognize, interpret, and anticipate hazardous traffic situations may contribute to reducing near-miss events and crash risks, providing practical implications for motorcycle safety education and hazard perception training among university students.

items.title: Sustainable Laboratories with Green Flow Chemistry and Novak’s Meaningful Learning
items.abstract: Abstract As flow chemistry emerges as a pivotal technology for achieving sustainable development goals (SDGs), integrating it into the undergraduate curriculum requires an understanding of the total student experience. This study applies Novak’s theory of meaningful learning to evaluate the cognitive, affective, and psychomotor experiences of 82 students in a green flow chemistry laboratory. Data from a 15-item Likert survey and open-ended responses reveal a strikingly asymmetric learning profile: while students reported high cognitive engagement (mean = 4.30) and strong intrigue with the equipment (mean = 4.49), their psychomotor confidence was markedly lower (mean = 3.60). Notably, students expressed high attraction to the equipment (positive affect) alongside persistent intimidation and low confidence in data-driven decision-making (psychomotor). These results suggest that while green chemistry principles serve as effective cognitive and affective anchors for student interest, the technical novelty of flow systems creates a psychomotor threshold that current single-session formats do not fully bridge. Our findings demonstrate that measuring only cognition and affect would obscure this bottleneck, underscoring the importance of independently assessing all three domains. We propose that prelab familiarization activities, distributed multisession exposure, and explicit linking of experimental steps to green chemistry principles can support the development of technically confident sustainable chemists.

items.title: System of motivational exercises at the adaptation stage in foreign language training of senior students at a non-linguistic (technical) university
items.abstract: The article discusses and justifies the application motivational exercises at the adaptation stage in professionally-oriented foreign-language training for undergraduate students at a technical university. The purpose of the article is to substantiate and experimentally confirm the effectiveness of integration motivational exercises at the adaptation stage in foreign-language training of students. The article notes that senior students who possess a high level of lexical competence in the terminology of a specific scientific field nonetheless have difficulty while confronted with the need to use interdisciplinary information in a foreign language, which requires the ability to interpret such information. The article presents a specially designed set of motivational exercises: training drills, ice-breakers, profession-focused communicative exercises, and developmental tasks. The methodology includes an analysis of scientific papers on the study of exercises in foreign language learning, integration of an adaptation stage into academic programs, diagnosis of personal characteristics and linguоcognitive abilities of students. The experiment demonstrated that an adaptation stage with exercises in predictive thinking and creativity (including elements of science fiction and artificial language) increases students’ readiness to innovation in a scientific environment. The results confirmed a statistically significant reduction of language anxiety by 29.01%, an increase in intrinsic motivation by 23.39% and rates of development of probabilistic forecasting by 27.87%, verbal creativity by 29.61%. Motivational exercises at the adaptation stage in professionally-oriented foreign language training of senior technical university students create an adaptive educational environment: it reduces language barriers; enhances intrinsic motivation; develops soft and cognitive skills and also dynamically adjusts the content and educational trajectory based on the results of continuous diagnosis.

items.title: Technostress and Worker Well-Being in the Platform Economy: An Integrative Literature Review
items.abstract: The rapid expansion of digital platform work has transformed how labour is organized, evaluated, and compensated, deepening workers' dependence on technology-mediated systems. This integrative literature review examines the relationship between technostress and worker well-being in the platform economy, with particular attention to algorithmic management. Drawing on 29 peer-reviewed sources identified through a structured search of academic databases and search engines, the review synthesizes evidence on techno-overload, techno-complexity, techno-insecurity, and techno-uncertainty alongside algorithmic monitoring, performance evaluation, scheduling, and compensation. Technology-related demands are consistently associated with emotional exhaustion, poorer well-being, work–life conflict, burnout, impaired productivity, reduced engagement, and intentions to discontinue platform work. These relationships are not uniform: worker appraisal, self-efficacy, personality, autonomy, transparency, fairness, and human influence shape how technological demands are experienced, while economic dependence and financial insecurity can intensify the consequences of algorithmic control by limiting workers' ability to reject undesirable conditions or exit platforms. The review conceptualizes platform worker well-being as a sociotechnical outcome arising from the interaction of digital demands, algorithmic governance, individual resources, and structural conditions, and proposes an integrated multilevel framework linking these elements. Gaps concerning longitudinal evidence, cross-platform comparison, measurement integration, geographic diversity, and platform-level interventions are identified, and a corresponding research agenda is outlined. The review contributes by connecting technostress theory with algorithmic-management and platform-dependence perspectives, and by arguing that improving platform worker well-being requires attention to platform design and governance rather than individual coping alone.

items.title: The Asymmetric Nature of Social Hierarchies: Unpacking the Dynamic Relationship Between Power and Status
items.abstract: Scholars and practitioners alike have long presumed that power and status, two foundational bases of social hierarchy, share a symmetric, mutually reinforcing relationship. However, support for this presumption has largely taken the form of theoretical accounts due to the prevalence of static research designs and a dearth of dynamic methodology in organizational research. Drawing on the Dual Perspective Model, we propose that one’s status is more likely to drive changes in one’s power than vice versa because status has a stronger connection to communion—an important component of interpersonal evaluations—than does power, and communality is an important predictor of both power and status. Using data from two studies involving project teams and a contemporary methodology from developmental psychology for modeling dynamic relationships (bivariate dual change score models), we illustrate that there is indeed a mutually reinforcing relationship between power and status over time, but this relationship is asymmetric. In three additional experiments, we find that perceptions of communality explain this asymmetry. We also find similar effects whether power is formal—attached to a position or role—or involves control over informal resources. Across all studies, we find that the path from status to changes in power is stronger than the path from power to changes in status.

items.title: The IDEA Design Scaffold: A Developmental Framework for Functional Ideation in Systemic Design
items.abstract: Abstract Functional ideation in systemic design unfolds within sociotechnical and sociocultural environments where goals, constraints, and evaluative criteria evolve across multiple levels of organization. Creativity research explains important aspects of novelty, variation, recombination, and selective retention, but it often treats novelty as emerging within a relatively stable representational space or a single level of abstraction. Systemic design scholarship, in turn, has developed strong approaches for framing complexity, mapping relations, organizing participation, and coordinating action, but it less often specifies how designers navigate between systemic levels, address challenges at different levels of abstraction, and construct intervention candidates while the task environment is still being differentiated. This paper responds by proposing a naturalistic framework of ideation within the Interactivist–Constructivist paradigm, with the IDEA Design Scaffold as its methodological architecture for systemic design. The central claim is that functional ideation under systemic complexity must be understood as a self-directed developmental process: intervention opportunities become novel and appropriate as designers navigate across levels of complexity through anticipatory exploration, partial stabilization, reflective reorganization, and rebuilding of missing supports. IDEAS operationalizes this account by linking Systemic Breakdown and Systemic Integration through the Iterative Innovation Cycle, enabling systemic goals, design challenges, and intervention candidates to be progressively coordinated without reducing ideation to a fixed procedure. The payoff is both theoretical and methodological: the paper explains why creative development in systemic design requires movement across levels of complexity, and provides an architecture for supporting, studying, and refining that movement in systemic design practice.

items.title: The Psychological Role Of The Borrowed Word “Insecure” In Shaping Classroom Engagement Among Young Efl Learners
items.abstract: Lexical borrowing has become a common phenomenon in English language learning. However, its psychological influence on young EFL learners remains underexplored, particularly regarding how borrowed words may relate to classroom engagement. Previous studies have examined lexical borrowing from linguistic and cognitive perspectives; however, little attention has been paid to its psychological and pedagogical implications in elementary school contexts. This study investigates students’ awareness of the borrowed word insecure and its role in shaping classroom engagement at MI Khadijah Malang. Employing a qualitative case study approach, the research involved 21 students from Grades Four, Five, and Six. Data were collected through classroom observations and semi-structured interviews and analyzed using thematic analysis. The findings reveal that students demonstrated different levels of awareness of the borrowed word insecure, with their understanding developing through exposure to English instruction, social media, peer interaction, and other everyday social environments. Students interpreted the term not only as an expression of low self-confidence but also as a reflection of academic comparison, anxiety, and self-improvement. Furthermore, the borrowed word was internalized in three distinct ways: as a source of motivation, as a form of self-doubt, and as having limited psychological influence. Interview and observation data showed that some students who associated insecure with self-improvement became more motivated, increased their learning effort, or developed new learning strategies, such as learning through songs, increasing vocabulary exposure, and using language-learning applications. In contrast, some students who compared themselves with higher-achieving peers experienced self-doubt and showed reduced participation or motivation, while others reported little influence from the term and maintained stable classroom participation. These different interpretations were associated with varying patterns of behavioral, emotional, and cognitive engagement in the English classroom. The study concludes that the relationship between the borrowed word insecure and classroom engagement is not uniform but varies according to how learners internalize and relate its meaning to their academic experiences and social interactions. By integrating lexical borrowing with learner engagement theory, this study demonstrates that borrowed words may function not only as linguistic resources but also as psychological labels that are associated with learners’ engagement in English language learning.
