items.title: The Relationship Between Personal Protective Equipment Comfort and Compliance with Personal Protective Equipment Use Among Workers at PT. Tasma Puja, Kampar Regency, in 2025
items.abstract: Labor compliance with the use of personal protective equipment can reduce the chances of work accidents and work-related diseases. In the industrial sector, it can be seen that many workers are reluctant or even not wearing PPE at all, this is due to several factors such as comfort, discomfort is one of the main reasons why workers do not use PPE according to standards, both in duration and how to use. This study aims to determine the relationship between the comfort of personal protective equipment (PPE) and compliance with the use of PPE in PT Tasma Puja workers in 2025. The research method used an observational analytical design with a cross sectional approach on 119 respondents from a population of 170 harvesters using simple random sampling. Data collection was carried out through a questionnaire and analyzed using the Chi-Square test. The results showed that there was a significant relationship between comfort and compliance with the use of PPE with a p value of 0.000. Most of the respondents are non-compliant and uncomfortable using PPE, so the lower the compliance of workers. The conclusion of this study shows that the comfort of PPE plays an important role in increasing worker compliance so that companies need to pay attention to ergonomics, quality, and comfort factors of PPE so that work safety increases and the number of work accidents in oil palm plantations can be reduced sustainably in the future. It is recommended that companies increase routine supervision and the application of sanctions and awards for workers, in order to increase the discipline of PPE use

items.title: The Strategic Role of Plant Layout in Lean Manufacturing: A Review of Principles, Digital Integration and Sectoral Applications
items.abstract: As the global manufacturing landscape undergoes rapid transformation, organizations are compelled to enhance productivity, reduce waste, and strengthen competitiveness. Lean manufacturing has emerged as a critical methodology to achieve these objectives, fundamentally shifting how businesses approach production by eliminating non-value-adding activities, pursuing continuous improvement, and utilizing resources efficiently. Within this paradigm, the design of plant layouts plays a pivotal role, serving as the foundation for operational efficiency through optimized workflow, reduced transportation, and effective space utilization. This review paper examines the multifaceted relationship between plant layout and lean manufacturing, tracing its evolution from the Toyota Production System to contemporary Industry 4.0-enabled smart factories. The paper explores foundational lean principles, various layout typologies, integration with lean tools such as 5S, Kaizen, and Kanban, and the emerging influence of digital technologies including digital twins, the Internet of Things, and artificial intelligence. Furthermore, it addresses human factors and ergonomics, environmental sustainability through green lean approaches, sector-specific applications, and persistent implementation challenges. By synthesizing insights from academic literature and industry case studies, this paper provides a strategic framework for researchers, practitioners, and policymakers seeking to leverage layout design as a driver of lean transformation and long-term operational excellence.

items.title: The viral deviation: a quantitative analysis of social media engagement metrics on non-compliant flight deck behaviors
items.abstract: Background Normalization of Deviance (NoD) is a well-documented organizational failure mode in aviation, yet its propagation through digital ecosystems remains unexplored. The European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) highlights a critical mentorship vacuum due to pilot retirements, and social media platforms increasingly serve as informal training environments. This study introduces the concept of Algorithmic Normalization of Deviance- ANoD, hypothesizing that recommendation algorithms systematically reward and amplify “gray-zone” cockpit behaviors that erode sterile flight deck protocols. Method We conducted a stratified netnographic analysis of 150 high-visibility aviation videos (N = 150) across Instagram Reels, split between algorithmically recommended content (n = 100) and curated influencer content (n = 50). A novel coding framework operationalized compliance (Compliant vs. Gray Zone vs. Deviant) and incentive structures. Engagement metrics were analyzed to quantify the algorithmic advantage of non-compliant behavior. Results The analysis reveals a directionally consistent “Viral Deviation” pattern rather than a statistically decisive one. Gray-zone recordings (i.e., technically legal but procedurally borderline) comprised 57% of the sample and attracted higher engagement than compliant content, although this difference was small and did not reach conventional significance (d = 0.24, p = 0.11). The clearest signal emerged between content sources: algorithmically surfaced posts showed significantly higher interaction rates than curated influencer posts (d = 0.31, p = 0.029), a small but statistically significant per-view advantage for content promoted directly by the recommendation system. Structural incentive analysis further indicates that monetization pressures co-occur with increased gray-zone production, structurally analogous to a parallel, shadow curriculum associated with conditions that may facilitate drift. Conclusion The study identifies statistical associations, not causal relationships, and the downstream behavioural impact on pilots is hypothesised from the algorithmic-pattern evidence rather than directly measured. Within those bounds, social media algorithms constitute a structurally unmonitored distribution channel whose observed associations with gray-zone content amplification are consistent with a normalisation-of-deviance feedback mechanism operating beyond current regulatory oversight — an association that warrants urgent empirical validation and proactive governance. We propose a shift from prohibition to risk-stratified governance, recommending that regulators distinguish between handheld (high-risk) and mounted (managed-risk) devices, and integrate digital algorithmic literacy into ab-initio pilot training to counter this new systemic threat.

items.title: Towards Responsible Mining in Africa: Problematising the Environmental and Public Health Concerns of Artisanal and Small‐Scale Gold Mining in Ghana
items.abstract: ABSTRACT There have been emerging media reports on the impact of cyanide and mercury use in artisanal and small‐scale gold mining (ASGM) operations on community health, especially among pregnant and non‐pregnant women, ASGM miners, and children in rural Africa. This paper gathers data from multiple sources, including media reports and qualitative research interviews, to critically examine and question the emerging environmental and public health concerns of ASGM operations in rural Africa, using Ghana, a country that has experienced a surge in illegal/informal mining activities over the past two decades, as a case study. Our findings revealed multifaceted and interrelated factors comprising (i) community exposure to heavy metals and disease contraction, (ii) congenital disabilities and pregnant women's exposure to toxic chemicals from ASGM operations, (iii) miners' exposure, disease burden and ill health, (iv) water‐related diseases, and (v) heavy metal bioaccumulation in food chains and associated with public health risks, as the growing environmental and public health risks and concerns of ASGM operations in Ghana. Based on these findings, we suggest a multidisciplinary socio‐ecological policy approach to mitigate the environmental risks and health concerns associated with ASGM operations in Ghana and, more broadly, across Africa. In this context, an integrated One Health approach that focuses on ASGM regulations, environmental management, occupational health and safety, public health, stakeholder engagement and community participation can be considered a suitable multidisciplinary socio‐ecological policy response. The policy and practical implications of our findings are discussed in the paper.

items.title: Turnover of agricultural land parcels in the context of the digitalization of government administration
items.abstract: This article examines the turnover of agricultural land plots in the context of the digitalization of public administration. It has been established that the management of land plots is not keeping pace with the rapid development of the digitalization of public administration; consequently, there is a need to improve the legislation governing the civil circulation of these plots. Issues related to the turnover of agricultural land remain relevant because proper regulation of this process allows for the optimization of relations between landowners, users, other individuals, local government bodies, and the state. The development of digital technologies in the field of public administration, on the one hand, allows for simplifying the process of land resource management; on the other hand, it requires additional measures from the state to ensure the proper protection of registries, the personal information of registry users, their uninterrupted operation, and so on. Taking into account the research conducted on the outlined issues concerning the management of agricultural land plots and the development of judicial practice in this area, the chosen field of study becomes a subject of both scientific and practical interest, and the development of proposals to improve the existing mechanism requires a balanced and comprehensively justified approach, since, as experience has shown, the digital technology sector is no less vulnerable to the human factor than the system currently in operation. The study found that current legislation needs to be updated to incorporate the latest advances in the digitization of public administration. When dealing with land plots in general and agricultural land plots in particular, digital technologies should be actively utilized to ensure the performance of all registration, analytical, monitoring, and other activities; to this end, appropriate amendments must be made to current legislation. The author’s vision for the implementation of mechanisms for the digitalization of public administration in the management of agricultural land is presented.

items.title: User Satisfaction With Assistive, Rehabilitation, and Training Technologies: Questionnaire Development and Content Validation Study
items.abstract: Background: According to human-centered design principles, user experience and user satisfaction are key aspects when developing or providing patients and clients with assistive, rehabilitation, or training technologies. Existing tools for assessing user experience and satisfaction are often either too narrow (developed for specific technologies) or too broad, failing to capture all relevant aspects of the technology being evaluated. Objective: The main objective of this study was to present the development process and content validation of a questionnaire that, following further validation steps, could be useful for researchers and developers in assessing the satisfaction of direct end users with assistive, rehabilitation, and training technologies. Methods: The development of the User Satisfaction Questionnaire for Assistive, Rehabilitation, and Training Technologies (U-ART-Q) followed a multistep process: (1) literature review, (2) domain definition and item generation, (3) expert consultation, (4) linguistic validation, and (5) content validation. Initially, 72 items were generated and organized into 7 domains. After expert review and linguistic validation, the questionnaire underwent content validation by 8 experts in physiotherapy, kinesiology, and ergonomics. Each item was rated for relevance using a 4-point Likert-type scale. The content validity ratio (CVR) and item-level content validity index (I-CVI) were calculated, and items below the accepted thresholds were removed or further revised. Results: Expert consultation resulted in the removal or merging of 20 items to improve clarity and reduce redundancy. Of the 52 items evaluated during content validation, 44 met the CVR and I-CVI criteria (CVR >0.75 and I-CVI >0.78). Eight items required additional review, and 2 items were ultimately removed. The final questionnaire comprises 10 initial screening questions and 50 content-valid items across 7 domains: design, comfort, effectiveness and usefulness, service, treatment or exercise, overall impressions, and safety. The overall average content validity index was 0.915, providing evidence of strong content validity. A macro-enabled Excel tool was developed to automate item selection and generate a PDF version of the questionnaire based on initial screening responses. Conclusions: The U-ART-Q is a newly developed instrument for assessing user satisfaction with assistive, rehabilitation, and training technologies. Further research will focus on psychometric evaluation, reliability testing, and multilingual validation to determine whether the U-ART-Q can provide a standardized method for assessing user satisfaction. Once fully evaluated, the questionnaire could support both developmental usability testing and postmarket evaluation, facilitating evidence-based decision-making and guiding future product improvement.

items.title: Using Customised LLM-Based Chatbots in Psychological Research: A Practical Tutorial
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based chatbots offer new methodological opportunities for psychological research by enabling scalable, standardised, and interactive research procedures. However, their usefulness depends on the researchers’ ability to customise, evaluate, and deploy them in ways that align with the methodological requirements of a given study. The current tutorial provides a practical, step-by-step framework for developing customised LLM-based chatbots for psychological research. We distinguish between no-code or low-code development approaches, including provider-hosted chatbot builders and visual or low-code programming platforms, and code-based approaches using proprietary model application programming interfaces (APIs) or locally hosted open-weight models. We compare these approaches in terms of technical expertise, behavioural and workflow control, study integration, cost, data governance, maintenance, and reproducibility. We also outline key components of the process of customising an LLM-based chatbot and illustrate deployment workflows across multiple platforms, including local desktop interfaces, messaging applications and survey platforms. Finally, we discuss key considerations for research ethics, privacy, data governance, security, transparency, and reproducibility, including recommendations for documenting and sharing chatbot configurations and study procedures. Through this tutorial, we aim to support researchers in integrating customised LLM-based chatbots into psychological research and in expanding the methodological possibilities available to them.

items.title: Virtual Reality Hypnosis: The Effectiveness of Virtual Reality Combined with Hypnotic Suggestions, a Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
items.abstract: Virtual reality (VR) is increasingly used to support physical and mental health interventions. Recently, VR combined with hypnotic suggestions, termed virtual reality hypnosis (VRH), has emerged as a promising approach across clinical and non-clinical settings. This systematic review and meta-analysis investigated the use and effectiveness of VRH. Searches were conducted in PubMed, Scopus, PsycINFO, and Embase following PRISMA guidelines. A total of 54 studies involving healthy and clinical populations were included. Meta-analytic results based on pre-post comparisons indicated a trend toward reduced anxiety following VRH (Hedges’ g = −1.39; 95% CI: −2.91 to 0.14). However, no significant differences were found when VRH was compared with other interventions, and no significant effects emerged for pain outcomes. Overall, VRH appears to be a promising intervention integrating immersive virtual environments with hypnotic suggestion, although further high-quality research is needed.

items.title: What occupational health challenges do hazmat truck drivers face? A network analysis and implications for safety management
items.abstract: Hazardous materials (hazmat) road transportation entails substantial safety risks, in which driver-related factors are consistently identified as the leading contributors to crashes. Yet the occupational profile, health status, and psychosocial resources of hazmat truck drivers remain poorly characterized, constraining the development of evidence-based safety management. To address this gap, this study surveyed 347 hazmat truck drivers in China, combining standardized scales with self-developed items capturing context-specific working experiences. These drivers were middle-aged (M = 42.52 years). The majority of them (87.6%) were overweight or obese. More than half of them were suffering musculoskeletal discomfort (58.8%) and suspected insomnia or insomnia (56.8%) together with daytime sleepiness. Although their self-reported fatigue was relatively low, sleep-related problems and physical health issues warrant particular attention. Network analysis further revealed two functionally distinct clusters within the work system: a physiological risk cluster (fatigue, insomnia, and daytime sleepiness) and a psychosocial resource cluster (perceived social support, professional identity, and subjective well-being). The associations between the two clusters were predominantly negative, suggesting a dynamic balance between occupational strain and adaptive resources. Subjective well-being, insomnia, and fatigue emerged as the most central nodes, indicating that they may serve as priority entry points for intervention. Our findings highlight that safeguarding the occupational health and safety of hazmat truck drivers requires an integrated and system-oriented management approach that jointly addresses physiological risks, psychosocial resources, and physical health. The study offers empirical evidence and practical implications for safety management in hazmat road transportation.

items.title: "The Error Behind the Error": Unravelling Human Factors in Dental Practice- A Narrative Review.
items.abstract: Abstract Human error is a natural part of complex healthcare systems, including dentistry. Dental care combines diagnostic reasoning, procedures, medication management, radiographs, infection control, lab work, digital tools, and teamwork. Errors can happen due to individual mistakes, but also to problems with communication, systems, equipment, processes, or the work environment. Research on dental patient safety has identified issues such as diagnostic and treatment-planning errors, communication breakdowns, medication incidents, procedural complications, wrong-site or wrong-tooth treatments, foreign-body aspiration or swallowing, and documentation problems. Modern patient safety science now recommends moving away from blaming individuals and instead focusing on system-based human factors. This review covers the main types of human error in dental practice, such as slips, lapses, mistakes, violations, active errors, and hidden risks. It also looks at factors that contribute to errors, including cognitive, technical, communication, environmental, technological, organizational, and patient-related issues. Prevention strategies include using standard protocols, safety checklists, clear communication, double-checking diagnoses, medication reviews, simulation training, incident reporting, root cause analysis, teamwork, and building a fair safety culture. The Swiss Cheese Model helps explain how multiple weaknesses in safety barriers can align and cause harm to patients. In the end, making dentistry safer means not just relying on individuals to be careful but also designing systems that account for human limitations, catch errors, and support learning within the organization. Keywords: Human error; Human factors; Dental practice; Patient safety; Dental errors.

items.title: "You Can't Just Automate It": Negotiating and Sustaining a "Good" Family Life Through Energy Practices
items.abstract: This study examines how Taiwanese parent-child families negotiate a "good" family life through everyday energy use and imagine future smart homes that support it. We conducted in-home interviews and co-design sessions with 21 families, including 46 parents and children. We found that families pursued a good life through energy practices shaped by thrift, comfort, care, safety, and enjoyment. These arrangements were continually adapted and responded to changing bodies, schedules, people, and infrastructures. This adaptive work was unevenly distributed, which in turn shaped different smart-home imaginaries. Drawing on the lens of Nearby and adversarial design, we conceptualize adaptation as situated sociotechnical work through which families continually rework energy arrangements. We further distinguish collective goods from plural and contestable goods to show why family IoT must support shared values while preserving opportunities to question and revise household arrangements. We offer theoretical and design directions for more adaptive, participatory, and contestable family IoT.

items.title: A Data-Driven Probability Hypothesis Density Filter with Parameter Flow Implementation for Space Situational Awareness
items.abstract: Abstract The Finite Sets Statistics-based Probability Hypothesis Density filter offers a description of a group of known or unknown targets as a single random entity with a Bayesian filtering framework. The Probability Hypothesis Density filter has often been employed in the Space Situational Awareness detection and tracking of space objects. One of its challenges is the determination of key probabilistic parameters, such as birth rates and birth intensities, for the detection of new space objects. Additionally, the challenge of incorporating nonlinear measurements requires the choice of simplifying assumptions on the prior, therefore introducing errors to the posterior. In this paper, a data-driven parameter flow version of the Probability Hypothesis Density filter is introduced, which performs the measurement update step using both birth and persistent likelihood densities while alleviating errors introduced to the posterior intensity. Therefore, preventing a shift of the birth intensity from the prediction step. A birth intensity is instantiated by performing a measurement correlation optimization, where the solution and likelihood are used to parametrize the intensity. In a data-driven discrete parameter flow Gaussian Mixture Probability Hypothesis Density filter implementation, the performance of the new birth is shown in a simulated ground-based optical tracking scenario. In optical tracking scenarios, tracklets composed of angles and angle rates are often assumed to be available. A multi-layer Probability Hypothesis Density filter is introduced, which forms tracklets before employing the full orbital data-driven Probability Hypothesis filter and the birth process. A Gaussian Mixture implementation of the multi-layer Probability Hypothesis filter is tested with a dataset for a GPS satellite collected from the Purdue Optical Ground Station.

items.title: A Hybrid Risk Assessment Approach Using Fine-Kinney Method and Fault Tree Analysis for Enhancing Laboratory Safety
items.abstract: To enhance laboratory safety, a risk assessment was conducted in environmental engineering laboratories using the Fine-Kinney Method (FKM) and Fault Tree Analysis (FTA). The FKM was initially employed to prioritize hazards, with a subsequent FTA used to systematically identify root causes and evaluate the effectiveness of existing controls. These two complementary approaches identified 10 risks, categorized into four groups: physical (electricity, fire, falling, sharp object injury), chemical (acid, poisoning, contamination), biological (infection, allergy), and ergonomic (musculoskeletal injury). Post-control measures successfully eliminated 89.3% of ‘Not Tolerated’ risks, contributing to an overall 63% reduction across all high-priority categories, including ‘Not Tolerated,’ ‘Strong,’ and ‘Important’ risks in FKM. Application of the FTA led to substantial risk reductions, with post-control measures decreasing hazard scores for fire, acid exposure, and electricity by 72.8%, 66.5%, and 60.0%, respectively. The statistical validation of the findings confirmed that the risk reductions achieved in both the FKM and FTA models were highly significant. The alignment of risk rankings across both models validated the assessment's reliability, providing a robust foundation for decision-making. Finally, implementing these validated safety measures requires a total budget of $42,000.

items.title: A Living Benchmark for Information Retrieval from Electronic Health Records
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based clinical assistants are increasingly being integrated into electronic health record (EHR) systems, transforming how clinicians retrieve and synthesize information from patient records. Their safety and utility depend on rigorous evaluation, yet existing benchmarks are manually curated, costly to update, and rapidly become obsolete with evolving technological advancements. We present a scalable framework that automatically generates question--answer pairs from longitudinal EHR notes. Nineteen clinicians validate the benchmark generator, producing the Benchmark for Retrieving Information in EHRs (BRIE), a continuously maintainable evaluation dataset. Across nine LLMs and five inference strategies, state-of-the-art systems frequently omit clinically important information, particularly for questions requiring synthesis across multiple documents and encounters. Because the generator itself is validated, BRIE supports evaluations that static benchmarks cannot, including the generation of multiple answers that reflect variation in clinician reasoning for robust performance assessment and continuously refreshing benchmark content to guard against leakage. Our results demonstrate that scalable benchmark generation enables rigorous, up-to-date evaluation of clinical LLMs as they are deployed in rapidly evolving healthcare settings.

items.title: A Multisensory Neural Evaluation Method for High-End Perception of Automotive Cockpits Based on Real-Vehicle Human Factors Experiments
items.abstract: Against the backdrop of accelerating premiumization among Chinese new energy vehicle brands, an objective measurement method for perceived luxury has become a critical methodological challenge for the industry. This study conducts in-vehicle human factors experiments using Rolls-Royce, Voyah Dreamer, and Zunjie as test vehicles, investigating the neural cognitive mechanisms and quantitative evaluation methods of cabin luxury perception across five sensory dimensions: somatosensory, tactile, olfactory, auditory, and visual. The experiment collects electroencephalogram (EEG), electrocardiogram (ECG), electrodermal activity (EDA), skin temperature (SKT), and eye-tracking data, which are integrated with subjective evaluations for comprehensive analysis. Based on these findings, this paper establishes a four-dimensional quantitative evaluation framework encompassing physiological arousal, EEG processing, behavioral responses, and subjective ratings, and proposes a sensory consistency threshold model to explain the nonlinear integration mechanism underlying overall perceptions of luxury.

items.title: A Paired Mixed-Effects Analysis of Lumbar Shear and Compression Forces in Manual Lifting
items.abstract: The Revised NIOSH Lifting Equation and the screening practices built around it interpret lumbar injury risk primarily through axial compression, yet anterior–posterior shear is associated with injury at loads below established compressive thresholds. L4 and L5 as are henceforth defined as the 4th and 5th lumbar vertebrae Using a harmonized database of 106 peak-loading lifting postures reconstructed through digital human modeling across five studies, we developed parallel families of linear mixed-effects regression models for L4/L5 compression and shear that shared identical predictor sets and matched random-effects structures, isolating biomechanical differences from differences in statistical specification. Load magnitude and horizontal hand reach acted as universal drivers of both outcomes—positive, highly significant, and stable across model reduction—although compression was several times more sensitive in absolute terms. The two components diverged in their posture sensitivities: knee flexion was significant only for shear, whereas trunk flexion, shoulder flexion, and vertical hand position acted predominantly on compression. Critically, no predictor significant in both families reversed sign, indicating that posture selectively modulates two independently sourced quantities—the moment arm of the supported mass, which governs compression, and the orientation of the lumbar segment, which governs shear—rather than redistributing a single conserved spinal reaction. Between-subject variability consistently exceeded between-task variability and persisted across model reduction, identifying individual lifting strategy as a structural determinant of spinal exposure. Among the 102 observations below the 3.4 kN compression criterion, 11 (10.8%) exceeded the lower 700 N shear reference, although none exceeded the upper 1000 N reference. Together these findings give a quantitative rationale for regarding compression-only assessment as structurally incomplete and support a multidimensional, posture-aware approach to ergonomic risk evaluation.

items.title: A questionnaire survey on context-dependent requirements for the trustworthiness of artificial intelligence and humans
items.abstract: Trustworthiness has become an important focus of artificial intelligence (AI) research. Although trustworthiness is a multifaceted concept and its requirements may depend on the context in which AI is used, little is known about how the public perceives these requirements. To address this issue, we conducted a questionnaire survey with nonexpert participants to examine the requirements that the public considers important for trustworthy AI and how their perceived value differs between social and nonsocial contexts. We further compared these context-dependent patterns with those observed for human trustworthiness. Our findings showed that, across social and nonsocial contexts, confidentiality and privacy protection were among the most important requirements for AI trustworthiness whereas the relative importance of other requirements depended on the context. In nonsocial contexts, transparency and interpretability of decision-making were particularly important whereas in social contexts, the ability to collaborate and communicate and a positive public image and attractive appearance were predominantly significant. Although similar context-dependent patterns were observed for human trustworthiness, findings consistently highlighted the ability to collaborate and communicate as a requirement for trusting humans, regardless of context, in contrast to AI trustworthiness. These findings provide insights into the public’s perception of trustworthy AI and highlight the importance of considering the context in which AI is used when examining AI trustworthiness requirements.

items.title: A Risk-Adaptive and Evidence-Constrained Framework for Generative AI Feedback in Programming Education
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence can turn learning analytics into personalized support, but feedback systems must decide when to intervene, which evidence to use, and how much assistance to provide. We developed a risk-adaptive, evidence-constrained framework for introductory programming using 2993 failed-submission states from 215 students. Student-disjoint models predicted persistent failure and related outcomes; four matched feedback conditions were generated for 136 cases; and calibrated risk informed capacity-limited intervention policies. The validation-selected logistic regression model achieved a test precision-recall area under the curve of 0.550 and a receiver operating characteristic area under the curve of 0.681. Broader student histories improved prediction of unmodified resubmission. After standardized repair and evidence gating, 519 of 544 newly generated messages contained all required components. A fixed-threshold sequential policy selected 17.8% of eligible test states and captured 25.2% of observed persistent failures. These findings support an evidence-gated progressive assistance strategy: calibrated risk guides intervention timing, recorded evidence constrains feedback content, and assistance progresses from self-checks to localized hints when warranted. The framework connects prediction, decision-making, and grounded generation while keeping their evaluation outcomes distinct.

items.title: A Unified Narrative Acceptance Model: Temporal Dynamics, Predictive Modulation, and Desensitization
items.abstract: This project presents the Unified Narrative Acceptance Model (UNAM), a formal and cross-disciplinary framework for explaining how humans accept or reject contradictions in both fictional narratives and real-world social situations. The model integrates cognitive science, narrative theory, and social psychology into a single inequality comparing an effective driving force with an effective resistance. Acceptance occurs when the driving force exceeds the resistance. UNAM distinguishes between Reader Mode (external evaluation of a narrative) and Actor Mode (internal evaluation by an agent embedded within a situation). The model incorporates temporal dynamics—including sunk-cost investment, self-narrative coherence, and desensitization—through saturating functions that capture long-term psychological changes. It also connects to predictive coding, interpreting contradictions as prediction errors modulated by reconstructability and precision weighting, and to narrative transportation theory, explaining how immersion amplifies emotional commitment. By unifying these mechanisms into a single formal expression, UNAM provides a structured account of narrative acceptance across contexts, offering a foundation for empirical studies, computational simulations, and applications in media analysis, social psychology, and human–AI interaction.

items.title: Aesthetic Processing Differences Between Representational and Defamiliarized Photographic Images During Initial and Repeated Presentations: Evidence from ERPs
items.abstract: Objectives: Repeated presentation may enhance processing fluency, but as novelty wanes, it may also reduce viewers’ cognitive engagement. Given that representational photographic images (RPIs) and defamiliarized photographic images (DPIs) differ in semantic clarity, it remains unclear whether repeated viewing differentially affects viewers’ explicit aesthetic judgments and neural processing during aesthetic judgments of these images. Methods: This study adopted event-related potentials (ERPs), and examined 40 participants’ aesthetic judgments of RPI and DPI during initial and repeated presentation. The behavioral measure was the proportion of images judged as “beautiful,” and ERP analyses focused on FN400 and early (500–1200 ms), mid (1200–3000 ms), and late (3000–5000 ms) LPP components. Results: Behavioral results showed that RPIs were judged as “beautiful” more often than DPIs, and presentation order did not significantly alter explicit aesthetic judgments. ERP results showed that repetition effects differed by image type: for RPIs, FN400 amplitudes were more positive and middle and late LPP amplitudes were reduced during the second presentation, whereas the repetition effect was not statistically significant for DPIs. Conclusions: Repeated presentation did not significantly alter explicit aesthetic judgments, but ERP repetition effects were observed mainly for RPIs and varied across processing stages. These preliminary findings suggest that the effects of repeated presentation on aesthetic judgments may be stage-dependent and stimulus-dependent. Future research should further disentangle presentation order from block order and more strictly match low-level visual features to test these effects.

items.title: AI and the layered evolution of information landscapes
items.abstract: The rapid adoption of generative AI has sparked debates about whether we are experiencing revolutionary disruption or evolutionary transformation of the information landscape. While headlines proclaim unprecedented changes, understanding AI's impact requires situating current developments within the evolution of how we have created, shared, and used information over centuries. We argue that generative AI represents not a radical break, but the latest interim layer in an evolving information landscape, progressing from pre‐digital systems through centralized computing, personal computing, the web, and social media. We outline the characteristics of each layer, including information infrastructures, information flows, and human roles. We discuss how layers have built upon predecessors while introducing novel challenges and opportunities: the web democratized publishing, social media enabled viral many‐to‐many networks, and generative AI now positions machines as co‐creators in hybrid intelligence systems. This means, rather than displacing earlier infrastructures, developments like generative AI add complexity to the information landscape, in which multiple layers coexist and interact. By recognizing both continuity and novelty in the evolution of our information infrastructure, we can more effectively navigate the generative AI era and ensure that technological advancement augments rather than replaces human agency, while preparing for the sociotechnical challenges it inevitably brings.

items.title: AI-Driven Decision Support for Disaster Management: Prioritizing Emergency Appeals using Computationally Efficient Deep Learning
items.abstract: Social media is an important lifeline in terms of real-time situational awareness in the aftermath of natural calamities. Nevertheless, emergency response teams are overwhelmed with information that they cannot process because of the general noise and actionable appeals. Although recent solutions in Deep Learning, namely, Bidirectional LSTMs (BiLSTM) and standard Transformers (BERT) exist, they are plagued by major drawbacks: RNNs are not always capable of capturing long-range semantic dependencies, whereas BERT models are not computationally efficient enough to be resorted to in resource-limited disaster areas. In order to fill this knowledge gap, this paper proposes Crisis-Connect, a computationally efficient decision support system that relies on a distilled Transformer architecture (DistilBERT). The model is benchmarked against traditional Machine learning (Naive Bayes), Recurrent Neural Networks (LSTM, GRU, BiLSTM), and Transformer models (BERT-Base). The experimental results on the HumAID dataset indicate that our framework gets an F1-score of 0.80, which is 5.2 percent higher than the RNN baseline without losing the performance of 95 percent of the teacher model. More importantly, the model incurs an inference latency of 1.46 ms, the model is 1.9x faster than standard LSTMs and 2.6x faster than BERT. Also, we use the Explainable AI (LIME) to confirm the model decision transparency. The present research has a role to play in the context of social innovation because it offers a low-latency, scalable tool that allows disaster management authorities to make data-driven decisions about edge devices without the use of high-end infrastructure.

items.title: AI-guided high-throughput discovery of iridium- and ruthenium-free palladium-oxide catalysts for durable acidic oxygen evolution
items.abstract: Catalyzing acidic oxygen evolution at the proton-exchange-membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) anode relies almost entirely on iridium or ruthenium, drawn from concentrated supply chains that constrain gigawatt-scale deployment. We report an artificial intelligence (AI)-guided, human-supervised closed-loop platform (>90% automation) integrating combinatorial sputter synthesis, high-throughput screening, machine-learning composition-property models, adaptive multi-objective optimization, and context-aware large-language-model reasoning, where lead catalysts advanced to long-term validation in 1 M H2SO4 at 10 mA cm-2. Navigating a combinatorial metal oxide space, the platform iteratively evaluated the activity-stability trade-off of 2,942 catalysts across 53 material systems and 26 elements, surfacing Ir- and Ru-free complex oxides such as InMnPdOx and NiTaPdOx that conventional design logic, and off-the-shelf language models, would not predict. In retrospective benchmarking, our sequential learning agent advanced the activity-stability frontier faster than fixed-policy Bayesian optimization or in-context language-model selection. During long-term testing, NiTaPdOx operated at lower overpotential than PdOx, but both eventually exceeded 0.5 V: PdOx at ~200 h and NiTaPdOx at ~470 h. InMnPdOx showed a similar overpotential improvement in addition to a dramatic increase in operational stability, retaining overpotential below 0.5 V over 1,000 h of operation. The additive elements promote the formation of a nanostructure that is associated with catalytic activity while stabilizing Pd against corrosion. The results highlight the power of AI-driven science in addressing long-standing challenges in materials chemistry, and the greater availability of Pd relative to incumbent Ir and Ru offers a near-term option to ease supply constraints on scaled electrochemical H2 generation.

items.title: AlphaDiverse: Post-Training Local Quantitative Research Agents for Diverse Exploration in Alpha Factor Mining
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems can automate alpha factor mining, but their reliance on external APIs limits control over cost, availability, and confidentiality. Long research loops also tend to revisit a few successful economic mechanisms that lead to research path collapse. To address these limitations, we propose AlphaDiverse, a framework that integrates a multi-agent alpha research system, diverse research path collection, and post-training for local agents. We let the research system generate complementary plan portfolios and vary research environments across loops to collect diverse research paths. Using these diverse traces, we warm-start local Planner and Realizer agents with supervised fine-tuning. Then, we propose a joint GRPO method to optimize both of them using predictive quality and diversity of contributions. Research feedback is confined to inner period data, while a frozen final model is evaluated on a later outer period data, thereby avoiding test-set tuning. Experiments across four Chinese stock universes show that AlphaDiverse can combine competitive prediction with broader exploration.

items.title: An Adaptive Human-in-the-Loop Generative AI Framework for Professional-Supported Pronunciation Exercise Design: Ex Ante Evaluation in Down Syndrome
items.abstract: Personalized pronunciation-exercise design requires flexible content, professional oversight, and mechanisms that can adapt recommendations without transferring therapeutic authority to artificial intelligence. This study presents Speak4All, a cloud-deployed human-in-the-loop generative AI framework designed to support professionals in preparing, personalizing, reviewing, and adapting pronunciation-oriented exercises. Although the platform can support pronunciation activities for primary-school children with different speech-related needs, the present evaluation focuses on contexts involving children with Down syndrome. Following a Design Science Research approach, the framework integrates structured profiles, professionally defined targets, longitudinal assessment history, interpretable difficulty recommendations, deterministic generation constraints, and explicit Accept/Modify/Reject control points. The study follows an ex ante evaluation strategy conducted before involving children as research participants. Two complementary scenarios were considered: an exploratory eight-participant stakeholder evaluation conducted at a volunteer center in Ecuador and a remote evaluation of the cloud-deployed system with 25 anonymous volunteers with relevant professional backgrounds, including special-education teachers working with children with Down syndrome. In the controlled evaluation, the adaptive framework achieved 84.8% acceptance without editing, 100.0% post-validation hard-constraint compliance, and 87.0% exact agreement between adaptive recommendations and independent professional judgments, with a weighted agreement coefficient of κw=0.848. The stakeholder evaluation provided complementary evidence of perceived personalization, usefulness, satisfaction, progress monitoring, and multimedia support. These findings support the technical feasibility and professional acceptability of the framework as a decision-support environment but do not establish clinical effectiveness or improvements in children’s speech. Future prospective studies should evaluate supervised use with children using validated speech-related outcome measures.

items.title: An Artificial Prefrontal Cortex for LLM Agents: A Structural Executive Module That Intercepts Jailbreaks, Collusion, Mutation Attempts and Long Horizon Evasion Tactics
items.abstract: Current attempts to instill internal alignment mechanisms into modern AI systems remain brittle when applied to autonomous, tool using agents facing out of distribution adversarial attacks, multi-step evasion strategies, and context smuggling. To date, none of the attempts at instilling internal alignment safety protocols have computationally modeled the approach developed by evolution to guide humans away from rogue behaviors and towards socially aligned ones. In human neurobiology, behavioral safety is enforced through hierarchical, intrinsic executive inhibition mediated by the prefrontal cortex (PFC). When PFC function is impaired by disease, trauma, or developmental conditions, disinhibition, poor judgment, and rule-violating behaviors emerge. Drawing on this biomimetic principle, we propose and prototype a structural containment framework-the Artificial Prefrontal Cortex (aPFC)-that provides an external layer of executive control over LLM based autonomous agents. Using Gemma 4-e4b and a Python based implementation, this pa- per presents a prototypical executive control architecture that remained robust under diverse adversarial conditions, including authority framing jailbreaks, multi node collusion, stealth payload mutation, context smug- gling, buffer flushing, and long horizon evasion. The architecture intro- duces a decoupled Executive Control module composed of four functional analogues inspired by human PFC organization: (1) a deterministic reflex layer providing zero latency constraint enforcement for known vulnera- bilities; (2) a coordination and perseveration detector that terminates unauthorized multi agent swarming and repeated evasion loops; (3) a se- mantic working memory evaluator that uses an LLM to assess the intent and consequences of proposed actions; and (4) an event driven temporal tracker that consolidates multi step behaviors to mitigate buffer flushing and “temporal amnesia” attacks. Empirical validation in an air-gapped simulation environment demon- strated that the system autonomously intercepted authority framing jail- breaks, multi node collusion, stealth payload mutations, and long horizon evasion tactics. These findings suggest that securing autonomous AI sys- tems requires moving beyond current internal model alignment and toward structural executive containment, providing a scalable and model agnostic blueprint for next generation AI safety.

items.title: Analyzing Human Centered Industrial Engineering Approaches in Improving Productivity and Employee Wellbeing in Modern Production Systems
items.abstract: Modern production systems increasingly rely on automation, digitalization, and advanced technologies to improve productivity, yet these developments may generate physical, cognitive, and psychosocial challenges for employees. This study aims to analyze human-centered industrial engineering approaches in improving productivity and employee wellbeing within modern production systems. A qualitative library research approach was employed by examining relevant books, peer-reviewed journal articles, scientific publications, research reports, and previous studies. Data were collected through systematic literature review and analyzed using content analysis to identify patterns, relationships, and key findings related to human-centered engineering, productivity, and employee wellbeing. The findings indicate that human-centered approaches can support productivity through improved work-system design, ergonomics, human–technology interaction, employee participation, and reduced physical and cognitive workload. At the same time, these approaches contribute to employee wellbeing by addressing physical, cognitive, and psychosocial factors. The study concludes that integrating human-centered principles into industrial engineering provides a sustainable pathway for jointly optimizing productivity and employee wellbeing in modern production systems.

items.abstract: ArGuard is a shared task on harmful content detection in Arabic memes and LLM prompts. It includes two tracks: Track A focuses on multimodal hate detection in Arabic memes, while Track B addresses harmful prompt detection for Arabic LLM safety evaluation. In total, 58 teams registered, 35 participated in the final evaluation, and 27 submitted system-description papers. Participating teams explored models such as AraBERT, Jais, and Qwen3-VL. The best systems achieved macro-F1 scores of 0.823 on A1, 0.419 on A2, 0.984 on B1, and 0.790 on B2. Fine-grained meme classification in A2 was the most challenging setting, partly due to sparse labels and train-test distribution shifts.

items.title: ARGUS: Role-Aware Event Knowledge Graphs for U.S. Employment-Discrimination Complaints
items.abstract: U.S. employment-discrimination complaints describe complex event sequences that are not explicitly captured by lexical or embedding-based representations alone. We present ARGUS, a source-grounded pipeline that combines a 5W1H-inspired schema, legal-domain models, and LLM-based structured generation to construct document-level Event Knowledge Graphs (EKGs) from CourtListener complaints. ARGUS extracts fact-bearing statements, builds chunk-level event graphs with participant, temporal, and causal structure, and merges them into document-level representations. We evaluate graph quality through human and multi-model assessment and test downstream utility on claim classification and legal QA. The graph-structured classifier outperforms raw and linearized baselines on the held-out set, and EKG-only retrieval improves document-scoped QA, while open-retrieval gains remain limited by low first-stage candidate recall. These results suggest that EKGs are most useful for organizing and reasoning over evidence once relevant material has been retrieved.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence and Digital Media Automation
items.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence into digital journalism has moved far beyond simple assistance. Algorithmic systems function as active participants in gathering, writing, and distributing news. This chapter investigates how technical imperatives, speed, scale, and measurability interact with professional journalistic values such as accuracy, fairness, and public accountability. Drawing on a multi-lens theoretical framework (institutional logics, sociotechnical systems, and audience trust models), the analysis shows that AI redefines the journalist's role, turning human workers into supervisors and validators of machine output. While automation enables impressive gains in data processing and routine reporting, it also introduces serious risks: algorithmic bias, lack of source transparency, and blurred lines of editorial responsibility. Audience research indicates that trust is not automatically lost when AI is used, but it depends heavily on visible, credible human oversight.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in HR Services and Employee Experience: The Role of Personalization and Organizational Digital Culture
items.abstract: The present study examines the role of AI-driven tools in influencing the employee experience quality, proposing a moderated mediation model that employed perceived personalization quality as mediator and organizational digital culture as moderator. Data were collected via a structured online survey from 491 executive managers, HR managers, HR specialist across medium to large organizations. A dual-stage analytical approach was employed: partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) and artificial neural network (ANN) analysis. AI-driven HR personalization notably enhances perceived personalization quality, which is positively related to employee experience quality. Perceived personalization quality mediates the relationship between AI-enabled HR personalization and employee experience quality. Organizational digital culture significantly strengthens the impact of AI-enabled HR personalization on perceived personalization quality, supporting its moderating role. This study adds value to the digital HRM literature by synthesizing resource-based view (RBV), technology acceptance model (TAM) and socio-technical systems (STS) theory in an integrated model.

items.title: Assessing the Validity of a Single-item Measure of Exposure to Workplace Bullying: A Mixed-Methods Study Among Swedish Workers
items.abstract: Abstract Importance Workplace bullying poses significant risks to mental and occupational health, highlighting the need for efficient measurement in surveys and large-scale observational studies. Objective The aim of this mixed-methods study was to evaluate the validity of the PP-item, a brief measure of personal persecution at work, used to assess workplace bullying, included in the Swedish Longitudinal Occupational Survey of Health (SLOSH). Methods Using two samples based on SLOSH 2008 and SLOSH 2023 (N=445 and N=1148, respectively), the theoretical properties of the PP-item were assessed through qualitative content analysis of self-reported experiences of personal persecution, while psychometric properties were evaluated by examining convergence with established measures, as well as examining its discriminant and predictive performance. Results We found that the PP-item captures experiences that reflect meaningful categories of bullying behaviours and that it showed moderate agreement with established measures of workplace bullying (self-labelling, κ=0.6; Negative Acts Questionnaire-Revised, κ=0.5). The PP-item was able to distinguish bullying from workplace violence and predicted subsequent symptoms of depression (odds ratio: 4.6, 95% confidence interval 2.5-8.7) and anxiety (odds ratio 3.1, 95% confidence interval 1.9-4.9) in an expected manner. However, the PP-item appeared more sensitive to person-related than work-related negative acts and potentially included also lower-threshold negative interactions, showing moderate correlations with workplace conflicts. Conclusions The findings from both quantitative and qualitative analyses support the PP-item as a valid tool for capturing exposure to negative workplace interactions, that are largely aligned with the theoretical construct of workplace bullying. Implications for practice While the overall findings support the validity of the PP-item, it may be useful to consider distinct features, such as exposure frequency and duration, when using the PP-item.

items.title: Association between students’ self-perceptions in physical education and out-of-school physical activity: the role of autonomous motivation
items.abstract: Both organized (OrPA) and unorganized physical activities (UnPA) offer known health benefits to adolescents. However, many youths are increasingly abandoning physical activity (PA). Research suggests that students’ self-perceptions in physical education (PE)—such as interest, perceived competence, and the value they assign to PE—may influence PA outside of school. Yet, it remains unclear whether these factors directly impact PA or do so through other variables, like autonomous motivation. This study explored whether autonomous motivation mediates the relationship between PE self-perceptions and engagement in OrPA and UnPA. A total of 1320 secondary students (average age 14.28) completed surveys measuring motivation and activity levels. Two mediation models were tested using the R Package GLM Mediation Model. Perceived competence was the only significant predictor of both OrPA and UnPA. Interest, importance, and tension had no direct effects. Both models showed full mediation through autonomous motivation, particularly via integrated and identified regulations. Intrinsic motivation was not a significant mediator. Findings suggest that students’ perceived competence in PE encourages out-of-school PA by enhancing motivation. PE teachers should promote self-awareness, educate on health benefits, and equip students to plan their own PA, thus fostering lasting motivation. Resumen Tanto las actividades físicas organizadas (OrPA) como las no organizadas (UnPA) ofrecen beneficios para la salud de los adolescentes. Sin embargo, muchos jóvenes abandonan cada vez más la actividad física (AF). Estudios sugieren que la percepción que los estudiantes tienen de la educación física (EF), como el interés, la competencia percibida y el valor que le asignan, puede influir en la AF fuera de la escuela. Sin embargo, aún no está claro si estos factores influyen directamente en la AF o lo hacen a través de otras variables, como la motivación autónoma. Este estudio quiere investigar si la motivación autónoma realiza un papel mediador entre las autopercepciones de la EF y la participación en OrPA y UnPA. Un total de 1320 estudiantes de secundaria (edad media de 14,28 años) completaron encuestas sobre niveles de motivación y AF. Se probaron dos modelos de mediación utilizando el paquete R GLM Mediation Model. La competencia percibida fue el único predictor significativo tanto de la OrPA como de la UnPA. El interés, la importancia y la tensión no tuvieron efectos directos. Ambos modelos mostraron una mediación completa a través de la motivación autónoma, en particular a través de regulaciones integradas e identificadas. La motivación intrínseca no fue un mediador significativo. Los resultados sugieren que la competencia percibida por los estudiantes en la educación física fomenta la AF fuera de la escuela al mejorar la motivación. Los profesores de educación física deberían promover la autoconciencia, educar sobre los beneficios para la salud y facilitar a los estudiantes herramientas para que planifiquen su propia AF, fomentando así una motivación duradera.

items.title: Asymmetric Dynamic Routing: Balancing Reasoning Depth and Computational Efficiency in Hypergraph RAG
items.abstract: While graph-based and hypergraph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) significantly mitigate hallucinations in Large Language Models (LLMs), existing structure-based RAG systems typically adopt static traversal strategies regardless of the query complexity. We identify this ``static retrieval fallacy'' as a primary source of computational redundancy for simple queries and cognitive context gaps for complex reasoning tasks. To balance reasoning quality and inference efficiency, we propose Asymmetric Dynamic Routing (ADR), an intent-conditioned retrieval framework operating over hierarchical knowledge graphs. ADR employs a lightweight structured classifier to dynamically dispatch queries among three asymmetric topological traversal operators: localized fact anchoring, bottom-up adjacency diffusion, and top-down insight grounding, which collectively enable bidirectional information flow across hierarchical knowledge layers. Extensive empirical evaluations across five domain-specific corpora demonstrate that ADR maintains strong reasoning performance while reducing prompt token consumption by up to 48.7\% and end-to-end query latency by 45.3\%, yielding a favorable quality--efficiency trade-off for query-adaptive Hypergraph RAG.

items.title: Attitude of dental students towards medical emergencies: About a survey of 306 FMDM students
items.abstract: Introduction: Medical emergencies in dental practice are serious, often unexpected, and can be life-threatening.Aim and Objectives: This study aimed to determine the prevalence of medical emergencies encountered by dental students at the Faculty of Dental Medicine of Monastir (FMDM) and to assess their attitudes and preparedness for managing these situations.Materials and Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 306 dental students in their 4th, 5th, and 6th years using a self-administered questionnaire. The survey covered socio-demographic, occupational, and ergonomic data.Results: 29% of students experienced medical emergencies during clinical training; 33% of cases involved vasovagal syncope, and 31% involved hypoglycemia. Among them, 45% sought help from seniors, and 39% reported performing first aid. On average, 73.09% felt concerned by medical emergencies. 59.44% believed they could provide first aid. Fifth-year students performed better than others. However, 62% of students believed that an Automated External Defibrillator (AED) is necessary, and 14% did not know its function. Only 20% had received additional training in first aid. Students with training were more capable of identifying emergencies and performing proper actions.Conclusion: Medical emergencies are relatively frequent in dental settings. While students receive adequate theoretical training, gaps remain in practical preparedness. Improved first aid training and clinical internships can enhance students’ competence in managing emergencies.

items.title: AUGMENTED, VIRTUAL AND MIXED REALITY IN ORAL AND MAXILLOFACIAL SURGERY: A REVIEW OF SURGICAL TRAINING, NAVIGATION AND PATIENT-CENTERED APPLICATIONS
items.abstract: Objectives. Augmented reality (AR), virtual reality (VR), and mixed reality (MR)-collectively termed extended reality (XR)-are increasingly applied in oral and maxillofacial surgery (OMFS), a discipline that combines anatomical complexity with high demands for precision and aesthetics. This review synthesises the current applications, reported performance, and limitations of AR, VR, and MR across four domains of OMFS: surgical training and simulation, preoperative planning, intraoperative navigation, and patient communication. Methods. A narrative, thematically structured review of peer-reviewed studies applying AR, VR, or MR to OMFS and closely related surgical fields was conducted, with findings organised by application domain and appraised against the metrics most often reported. Results. In training, immersive VR and haptic simulators provide risk-free, repeatable, objectively assessed practice and yield outcomes that are non-inferior and often superior to conventional methods. In planning, immersive three-dimensional visualisation improves spatial understanding and supports waferless, guide-based, and patient-specific workflows. In navigation, AR and MR overlay the surgical plan onto the operative field, with reported overlay or registration errors typically in the sub-millimetre to low-millimetre range. In patient communication, patient-specific VR, AR, and MR visualisations improve understanding and satisfaction and reduce anxiety during informed consent. Conclusions. XR offers tangible benefits across the OMFS pathway, yet evidence is constrained by small heterogeneous studies, registration and ergonomic challenges, novelty bias, and limited long-term clinical data. Robust validation, cost-effectiveness analysis, and standardised reporting are needed before routine adoption.

items.title: Back to the Definition: Estimating Step-Level Advantages via Trajectory Graphs for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
items.abstract: Group-based reinforcement learning (RL) methods, such as GRPO and its variants, have become a leading paradigm for training reasoning and agentic large language models (LLMs). While their group-normalized advantage estimation is reliable at the response level, it becomes systematically biased at the step level, since coarse-grained trajectory-level advantages are hard to accurately reflect the contribution of individual steps (i.e, failed trajectories may contain valuable steps). Revisiting the foundational RL definition, we notice that GRPO's success on single-turn tasks stems from its advantage estimation strategy, which adheres to the basic definition: the mean reward of multiple actions sampled from the same state constitutes a credible state-value estimate. Extending the faithful estimation to step-level would in principle demand sampling multiple actions from each intermediate state, which is too costly on a per-state basis. To mitigate this issue, we propose a Graph-based Faithful sTep-level credit-assignment framework (GRAFT) that grafts all rollout trajectories into a trajectory graph, recovering node state-values via Bellman iteration on the graph, and assigning credit to each edge by the node value difference. Theoretically, the estimated step-level advantage faithfully adheres to the basic advantage definition in RL. To further ensure the reliability of step-level advantage estimation, we further propose Graph GAE, which extends GAE to the trajectory graph for reducing the impact of state-value estimation bias. Experiments across a range of multi-turn agentic benchmarks show consistent gains over GRPO and superior performance compared to recent agentic RL algorithms. Code will be available at https://github.com/xcyao00/GRAFT.

items.title: BanglaTurn: A Benchmark and Whisper-Based Model for End-of-Turn Detection in Bangla Speech
items.abstract: This paper presents BanglaTurn, a corpus for end-of-turn detection in Bangla conversational speech, and a model trained on it. The corpus holds 35,374 samples of 3 to 15 s of podcast speech, labelled for turn state by combining speaker diarization with an LLM pass, with every label then checked by a human annotator. The model pairs a Whisper encoder with task-specific classification heads. On a class-balanced test set drawn from a held-out podcast, it reaches 84.33% accuracy (95% CI 80.3 to 88.1) against 69.28% for the Smart-Turn v3 baseline, and lowers the false negative rate from 51.57% to 7.55% at the cost of a higher false positive rate. We report what encoder layer fine-tuning, multi-scale pooling and INT8 quantization each contribute, and latency stays within 165 to 191 ms end to end on CPU.
